one_line_description: Cloud CRM and enterprise platform offering sales, service, marketing, commerce, and automation APIs.
auth_details: Salesforce REST and related APIs use OAuth authentication via connected apps. Docs reference OAuth scopes and passing access tokens in the Authorization header. Account Engagement API additionally requires a Pardot-Business-Unit-Id header.
self_serve_detail: Salesforce provides a public developer portal and developer sign-up flows. API access availability depends on edition; some editions require paid API access. Developer environments appear self-serve.
api_breadth_detail: Salesforce exposes extensive APIs across CRM, marketing, commerce, metadata, and platform services. Developer portal links to REST API, Marketing Cloud APIs, Metadata API, Commerce APIs, and many product-specific APIs covering most platform capabilities.
mcp_server_detail: Salesforce provides official Hosted MCP Servers documentation for connecting AI agents to Salesforce via MCP and OAuth. There is also a community MCP Salesforce connector on GitHub supporting SOQL/SOSL queries and CRUD operations. Official docs: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/hosted-mcp-servers-overview.html Community server: https://github.com/smn2gnt/MCP-Salesforce
buildability_detail: Salesforce has mature public APIs, standard OAuth authentication, broad API coverage, self-serve developer access, and official MCP support. Some enterprise editions may require paid API access, but overall the platform is suitable for building an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: CRM and sales platform offering marketing, sales, service, and customer data management tools.
auth_details: HubSpot supports OAuth authentication for public apps, private app access tokens using Bearer authorization headers, and developer API keys/static auth for certain developer APIs. Docs also reference client credentials OAuth flows.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create free HubSpot accounts and developer accounts with API access and testing environments. Public pricing page offers free CRM tools, and community discussion notes free-tier API access for testing.
api_breadth_detail: HubSpot exposes extensive REST APIs covering CRM objects, conversations, webhooks, marketing, sales, developer tooling, and more across many product areas.
mcp_server_detail: HubSpot officially provides MCP servers for CRM access and developer platform tooling: https://developers.hubspot.com/ai-tools/mcp . There is also a community MCP server at https://github.com/baryhuang/mcp-hubspot.
buildability_detail: HubSpot has a mature public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding with free access, standard OAuth/token authentication, and official MCP support, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: CRM and sales platform with APIs and developer tools for integrations and marketplace apps.
auth_details: Pipedrive supports OAuth 2.0 for marketplace/public apps and API token authentication via the x-api-token header for direct integrations. OAuth flow returns access and refresh tokens after authorization code exchange.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for a Sandbox Account on the Pipedrive Developers Corner to experiment and develop integrations. Public developer docs and API clients are available without sales contact.
api_breadth_detail: RESTful API with v1 and v2 endpoints, OpenAPI specifications, webhooks, OAuth support, and coverage across CRM resources such as deals, contacts, activities, and marketplace apps. Documentation suggests extensive platform coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Both community and official MCP servers exist. Community server: https://mcp.so/server/pipedrive-mcp-server/WillDent . Official native MCP server announced by Pipedrive enabling AI assistants to interact with CRM data in real time: https://www.destinationcrm.com/Articles/CRM-News/CRM-Across-the-Wire/Pipedrive-Launches-Native-MCP-Server-175523.aspx
buildability_detail: Pipedrive provides a public REST API with standard OAuth2 and API token authentication, self-serve developer sandbox access, OpenAPI specs, and broad CRM coverage, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: AI-native CRM platform for managing customer relationships, workflows, pipelines, and sales operations.
auth_details: Attio MCP documentation states the hosted MCP server uses OAuth authentication with Attio account login. Community MCP server references Attio API keys for authentication. Direct public API auth details were not clearly provided in the search results.
self_serve_detail: Attio offers a free plan and states 'Start today, no credit card required' on pricing page. Search results also mention free tier availability. However, one third-party article claims API access may require approval.
api_breadth_detail: Search results and MCP descriptions indicate broad CRM coverage including people, companies, deals, tasks, lists, notes, records, workflows, and CRUD operations across the workspace.
mcp_server_detail: Official hosted MCP server documented by Attio at https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview using OAuth authentication and supporting full workspace access. Community MCP server also exists at https://github.com/kesslerio/attio-mcp-server claiming comprehensive CRM surface coverage and full CRUD support.
buildability_blocker: API access approval ambiguity
buildability_detail: Attio appears to have a public developer platform, official MCP server, and self-serve signup with free tier. However, the provided results do not include direct public API authentication/reference docs, and one third-party pricing article claims API access requires approval, creating some uncertainty around immediate unrestricted developer access.

one_line_description: Open-source CRM platform with generated REST and GraphQL APIs per workspace schema.
auth_details: Developers create API keys in Settings → API & Webhooks → + Create key. Requests authenticate using the generated API key for both REST and GraphQL APIs.
self_serve_detail: API keys can be self-generated from within the Twenty app under Settings → API & Webhooks after creating a workspace/account. Search results did not indicate any sales or partnership approval requirement.
api_breadth_detail: Twenty generates workspace-specific REST and GraphQL APIs covering CRUD for built-in CRM objects (People, Companies, Opportunities) and custom objects. GraphQL supports batch upserts and relation traversal; both APIs support batching up to 60 records per request.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP server exists: 'Twenty MCP Server' on LobeHub backed by GitHub repository igorwarzocha/twenty-mcp-server. It integrates with Twenty CRM via GraphQL and REST APIs using TWENTY_API_URL and TWENTY_API_KEY environment variables. URL: https://lobehub.com/mcp/igorwarzocha-twenty-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Twenty exposes public REST and GraphQL APIs with self-serve API key generation and broad CRM object coverage, making it feasible for Composio to build an agent toolkit today. Community MCP ecosystem support also exists.

one_line_description: Work management and CRM collaboration platform with customizable apps and workflows.
auth_details: Podio API requires application registration and returns access tokens/refresh tokens for authenticated requests. Docs describe OAuth-style flows with access_token and refresh_token, plus username/password flow and app authentication flow using app ID and app token. API keys can be generated in user settings.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up or sign in to Podio and generate API keys themselves. FAQ states the API is free to use for both free and premium accounts with the same rate limits.
api_breadth_detail: Public REST API with authentication flows, app/item/task/contact access and broad platform coverage through many documented endpoints and resources.
mcp_server_detail: Official Podio MCP server documented by ShareFile/Podio. Server available at https://mcp.podio.com and supports AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, and Microsoft Copilot Studio. Docs: https://docs.sharefile.com/en-us/podio/using-podio/general-features/podio-mcp-server.html
buildability_detail: Podio provides a public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding with free access, standard token-based authentication flows, and even an official MCP server, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit.

one_line_description: Customer relationship management platform with sales automation, developer tools, and REST APIs.
auth_details: Zoho CRM API uses OAuth 2.0 authentication with authorization code/grant token flow to obtain access and refresh tokens. API requests use access tokens for authenticated access.
self_serve_detail: Zoho offers a free Developer Edition for developers to test and build integrations. Developers can sign up directly via the Zoho Developers website without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: Zoho CRM provides extensive REST APIs and SDKs covering CRM modules, records, queries, workflows, widgets, serverless functions, and integrations across the CRM platform.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Zoho CRM, including an open-source GitHub project (junnaisystems/zoho-crm-mcp) supporting OAuth authentication and operations such as querying, creating, updating, and searching CRM records. Additional MCP listing available on AIBase.
buildability_detail: Zoho CRM has a public REST API with standard OAuth2 authentication and self-serve developer access via a free Developer Edition, making it feasible for Composio to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: CRM and sales engagement platform for managing leads, contacts, opportunities, and communications.
auth_details: Close supports OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with client ID/client secret, redirect URI, access tokens, refresh tokens, and Bearer token authentication. It also supports API keys managed in account settings and used via HTTP Basic authentication with the API key as the username.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create and manage API keys directly in their Close account under Settings → Developer → API Keys. OAuth apps can also be created to obtain client credentials. No evidence of partnership or sales approval requirement was found.
api_breadth_detail: Close provides a REST API with resources for leads, contacts, opportunities, activities, custom fields, and more. Documentation references predictable REST endpoints, JSON request/response bodies, and an OpenAPI spec, indicating broad coverage of CRM functionality.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for Close was found in the provided search results.
buildability_detail: Close exposes a public REST API with standard OAuth2 and API key authentication. Developers can self-serve API credentials from within their accounts, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: CRM platform with a developer API for accessing and integrating Copper resources.
auth_details: Copper Developer API supports API keys with token-based authentication and OAuth2.0. API key requests require headers including the token and user email. Another developer portal example shows Authorization header with API key plus X-Signature HMAC signature and X-Timestamp headers.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access public developer documentation and generate API keys from the Copper web app under System settings > API Keys. OAuth2 apps can be registered by providing application details and callback URL. No evidence of partnership approval required was found.
api_breadth_detail: Copper provides a RESTful JSON API covering most Copper resources and integrations. Documentation describes access to most Copper resources through the Developer API endpoint and includes Postman collections.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server specific to Copper was found in the provided search results.
buildability_detail: Copper has a public REST API with standard authentication methods (OAuth2 and API keys), public developer documentation, and self-serve credential generation, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: CRM and deal management platform with REST APIs for authentication, schema, data, and publication/event operations.
auth_details: Docs show use of client_id and client_secret/apiKey credentials to obtain tokens for API access. API keys can be enabled from the user profile after appropriate permissions are granted. Authentication endpoints provide tokens for other APIs.
self_serve_detail: API access depends on having a DealCloud account with appropriate admin/user-group permissions. Docs mention contacting an organization's admin or DealCloud Customer Success Manager if permissions are unavailable. No public free tier or instant self-serve developer signup was found.
api_breadth_detail: Comprehensive REST API with Swagger/OpenAPI support covering authentication, schema discovery, data manipulation, and publication/event APIs across multiple endpoint groups.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for DealCloud was found in the results. The Workato page references integrations between Deal Cloud and MCP but is not itself an MCP server implementation.
buildability_blocker: API access requires existing DealCloud account permissions/admin enablement.
buildability_detail: DealCloud exposes a documented REST API with Swagger/OpenAPI and API key/client secret authentication, so toolkit development is technically feasible. However, obtaining credentials appears tied to enterprise account access and admin permissions rather than open self-serve developer onboarding.

one_line_description: Customer service and helpdesk SaaS platform with support, chat, voice, and AI agent capabilities.
auth_details: Search results mention secure authentication with Zendesk API tokens for MCP integrations. Zendesk developer APIs are referenced broadly, but exact OAuth flow details are not included in the provided results.
self_serve_detail: Zendesk offers a 14-day free trial with access to Suite Professional plan features, allowing developers to sign up without contacting sales for basic access.
api_breadth_detail: Search results and MCP server descriptions indicate broad API coverage across Zendesk Support, Talk, Chat, and Guide products, including tickets, users, organizations, comments, and help center/article management.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist for Zendesk, including https://github.com/mattcoatsworth/zendesk-mcp-server and https://github.com/reminia/zendesk-mcp-server. They provide comprehensive Zendesk API integrations for tickets, comments, users, Support, Talk, Chat, and Guide.
buildability_detail: Zendesk appears to have a public developer API ecosystem, self-serve trial access, standard token/OAuth-style authentication, and existing MCP implementations demonstrating practical integration feasibility.

one_line_description: Customer support and helpdesk platform with messaging, ticketing, and AI support tools.
auth_details: Intercom supports OAuth for public apps accessing other users' Intercom data, and access tokens for private apps accessing a developer's own workspace. Access tokens are generated in the Developer Hub and treated like passwords.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a free development workspace and set up apps directly through the Intercom Developer Platform to obtain API access tokens and test integrations without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: Intercom provides a versioned REST API (v2.15 referenced) with extensive coverage across admins, contacts, conversations, tickets, help center, workflows, reporting exports, messages, Fin AI, teams, tags, and more. Documentation indicates a large OpenAPI-generated API surface.
mcp_server_detail: Intercom hosts an official remote MCP server at https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp. GitHub repository and marketplace listings describe support for secure access to Intercom conversations, contacts, and other data via MCP with 6 available tools. Repository: https://github.com/intercom/intercom-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Intercom has a public REST API with standard OAuth and token authentication, self-serve developer onboarding, broad API coverage, and official MCP server support, making it suitable for Composio toolkit integration today.

one_line_description: Customer support and helpdesk platform for managing tickets, contacts, knowledge bases, and support workflows.
auth_details: Freshdesk developer discussions reference creating OAuth client apps with client ID and secret for integrations. Freshservice API examples show HTTP Basic authentication using either username/password or API key as the username with placeholder password. Freshdesk API docs are REST-based and historically support API key authentication.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access public developer docs and sign up for Freshdesk plans with a free plan and free trials available. No partnership approval is indicated for API access.
api_breadth_detail: Extensive REST API covering tickets, contacts/users, conversations, ticket fields, forms, companies, agents, forums, solutions/knowledge base, watchers, time entries, bulk operations, and admin resources across many endpoints.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Freshdesk, including freshdeck-mcp on mcpservers.org and the GitHub project NeuraLegion/freshdesk_mcp providing 41 tools for tickets, contacts, companies, conversations, and more via Freshdesk API v2. No official Freshdesk MCP server found in results, though Freshservice has an official Freshworks MCP integration EAP.
buildability_detail: Freshdesk exposes a broad public REST API with self-serve developer access and standard authentication methods (OAuth and API keys/basic auth). Existing community MCP implementations further indicate the API is practical for agent tooling today.

one_line_description: Customer communication and helpdesk platform for managing shared inboxes and support workflows.
auth_details: Front Core API authenticates with Bearer tokens sent in the Authorization header. Bearer tokens can be obtained either via manually generated API tokens in settings or through OAuth integrations using the Front application framework and App Store.
self_serve_detail: Front provides a free developer environment/account for building with the APIs. Developers can create a free developer account via the Developer Portal without sales involvement. Developer accounts are limited to 3 teammates.
api_breadth_detail: Front exposes a Core REST API covering most Front entities and workflows including contacts, comments, conversations, and other platform resources via the api2.frontapp.com endpoint.
mcp_server_detail: A community-created MCP server for FrontApp is discussed in the Front community forum, but no official MCP server was identified from the search results. Community thread: https://community.front.com/developer-discussion-39/is-anyone-working-on-creating-an-mcp-server-for-frontapp-2309
buildability_detail: Front has a public REST API, supports standard OAuth2 and bearer token authentication, and offers self-serve free developer accounts/environments, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Customer support and helpdesk platform with API and MCP integrations for managing issues, accounts, contacts, and workflows.
auth_details: The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication with API tokens generated in the Pylon dashboard. Only Admin users can create API tokens. The Pylon MCP Server authenticates AI tools via OAuth against the user's Pylon account.
self_serve_detail: Developers with Admin access in a Pylon account can self-generate API tokens from the dashboard. Public developer documentation is available. No explicit free tier information was found in the provided results.
api_breadth_detail: JSON-based web API supporting read/write access to Pylon data, including issues, accounts, contacts, users, leads, projects, webhooks, and deep-linking workflows. Documentation references API reference endpoints and automation use cases.
mcp_server_detail: Official Pylon MCP Server documented by Pylon. It exposes Pylon data and actions to AI tools via Model Context Protocol, supporting read/write operations on issues, accounts, and contacts with OAuth authentication. Docs: https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/pylon-mcp
buildability_blocker: API token creation restricted to Admin users; free/self-serve developer tier unclear.
buildability_detail: Pylon has a documented public REST API with bearer token authentication and an official MCP server. Composio could likely build an integration today, but access depends on having a Pylon account with Admin privileges to generate tokens, and the availability of a free developer tier is unclear from the provided results.

one_line_description: Customer support and helpdesk platform with live chat, ticketing, and multichannel support.
auth_details: REST API authentication uses an API key obtained from the LiveAgent account configuration/API settings page. API docs reference authentication failures caused by invalid API keys.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for a 30-day free trial and there is also a free pricing tier mentioned. API keys can be generated from the account settings without partnership approval.
api_breadth_detail: REST API v1 appears to cover a large portion of the platform including agents, tickets, calls, companies, API keys, and other helpdesk resources with many endpoints documented in the API reference and SDK repository.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server specific to LiveAgent was found in the provided search results.
buildability_detail: LiveAgent provides a public REST API with self-serve account creation and API key authentication, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Customer support and helpdesk platform with a GraphQL API for integrations.
auth_details: Plain GraphQL API uses API keys for authentication; docs mention creating an API key and storing it securely, with feature permissions documented per endpoint/feature.
self_serve_detail: Developer documentation is publicly accessible and authentication docs describe creating an API key directly. No evidence in provided results of sales approval or partnership gating for API credentials.
api_breadth_detail: Public GraphQL API documented by Plain. Exact endpoint count is unknown from provided results, but authentication docs reference permissions for different features, suggesting coverage across multiple product capabilities.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for Plain was found in the provided search results.
buildability_detail: Plain appears to offer a public GraphQL API with self-serve API key authentication documented publicly, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Customer support and helpdesk platform with shared inboxes, knowledge base, and live chat tools.
auth_details: Mailbox API uses OAuth 2.0 with Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows. Developers create OAuth apps in Help Scout. Docs API uses per-user API keys passed via HTTP Basic Authentication username field. MCP examples mention Bearer personal access tokens.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create Help Scout accounts directly and the pricing page includes a Free plan with 5 users, 1 Inbox, and 1 Docs site. OAuth apps can be created from the user profile ('My apps'). Docs API keys can be generated from profile authentication settings.
api_breadth_detail: Help Scout exposes multiple REST APIs including the Mailbox API and Docs API covering conversations, mailboxes, users, workflows, collections, and knowledge base resources. Search results indicate broad operational coverage across support workflows.
mcp_server_detail: Community and third-party MCP servers exist. Example: 'Help Scout MCP Server' on mcp.so provides conversation search, customer profiles, mailbox management, analytics, OAuth2 and token auth support. StackOne also provides a hosted Help Scout MCP server with 36 actions. Sources: https://mcp.so/server/help-scout-mcp-server/drewburchfield and https://www.stackone.com/connectors/helpscout/mcp
buildability_detail: Help Scout has public REST APIs, standard OAuth2 authentication, self-serve developer onboarding via free accounts and app creation, and broad API coverage suitable for building an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Customer support and helpdesk platform with APIs for tickets, conversations, contacts, and helpdesk operations.
auth_details: Gorgias REST API uses HTTP Basic Authentication with a base API URL, email address as username, and API key as password. For public apps, Gorgias requires OAuth2 authentication with client_id/client_secret and authorization code flow.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access REST API credentials directly from their Gorgias account settings (Settings → You → REST API). Search results also reference a 30-day free trial on all plans.
api_breadth_detail: Gorgias exposes an open REST API for reading and writing helpdesk data, including tickets, conversations, contacts, analytics, and operational resources. Documentation suggests broad platform coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Official Gorgias MCP app/server exists. Gorgias documentation describes connecting AI assistants via MCP to access helpdesk data and settings. Community listings and Composio integration pages also reference the Gorgias MCP server. Sources: https://docs.gorgias.com/en-US/connect-your-ai-assistant-to-the-gorgias-mcp-6310546 and https://mcpmarket.com/server/gorgias
buildability_detail: Gorgias provides a public REST API with self-serve credential access and standard authentication methods (Basic auth/API keys and OAuth2 for apps). Official MCP support further improves integration readiness.

one_line_description: Customer service and helpdesk platform with APIs, SDKs, webhooks, and integrations for support workflows.
auth_details: Gladly APIs use API tokens generated within the Gladly UI by users with the 'API User' permission/role. Tokens are associated with an agent profile and used to access Gladly API resources.
self_serve_detail: API access appears tied to an existing Gladly organization/account. Sandbox environments require contacting a Gladly CSM or Support team to purchase/setup. No evidence of a public free developer tier or instant self-service signup for API credentials was found.
api_breadth_detail: Gladly exposes REST APIs, webhooks, SDKs, and platform integrations covering customer profiles, timelines, orders, Help Center configuration, chat SDK embedding, exports, and third-party integrations.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for Gladly was found in the provided search results.
buildability_blocker: API access tied to existing Gladly account and sandbox/setup may require contacting support or purchasing access.
buildability_detail: Gladly has a public REST API and token-based authentication with broad platform coverage. However, developer onboarding does not appear fully self-serve, and sandbox/API setup may require an existing customer relationship or support engagement.

one_line_description: Team communication and collaboration platform with messaging, workflows, and app integrations.
auth_details: Slack apps use OAuth 2.0 v2 installation flow to obtain access tokens with scoped permissions. Apps authenticate API access using Slack access tokens (bot/user tokens).
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign in with a Slack account and create applications through the Slack API apps portal. Slack API usage for building apps is described as free.
api_breadth_detail: Slack provides extensive developer APIs and SDKs covering messaging, channels, workflows, users, canvases, apps, and workspace interactions. Documentation includes multiple SDKs and CLI tooling indicating broad platform coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Slack provides an official Slack MCP server documented by Slack Developer Docs. It supports searching channels, retrieving and sending messages, managing canvases, and managing users through MCP clients. Community MCP servers also exist.
buildability_detail: Slack has a public developer platform with self-serve app creation, OAuth2 authentication, broad REST APIs, SDKs, and official MCP server support, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Cloud communications platform providing APIs for messaging, voice, video, email, authentication, and customer engagement.
auth_details: Twilio supports HTTP Basic authentication for REST APIs using an API key as the username and API key secret as the password. For local testing, developers can use Account SID as username and Auth Token as password. Twilio recommends API keys for production apps.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-sign up and start for free with usage-based pricing. Multiple Twilio products and APIs are marked 'Start for free' on the pricing page.
api_breadth_detail: Twilio exposes extensive REST APIs across communications products including messaging, voice, video, email, Segment, authentication, workflows, and more. The MCP documentation references over 1,800 endpoints across 30+ products, indicating very broad API coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Official Twilio MCP server exists and is documented by Twilio. Public Beta MCP server exposes Twilio's full API surface (over 1,800 endpoints across 30+ products). Hosted at mcp.twilio.com/docs, with additional official monorepo references on mcpservers.org.
buildability_detail: Twilio has a mature public REST API, standard authentication methods, self-serve developer onboarding with free access, extensive documentation, and even an official MCP server. Composio could build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Team messaging and collaboration platform with bots, commands, and automation capabilities.
auth_details: Zoho APIs use OAuth2 via the Zoho Developer Console to obtain access and refresh tokens; requests use Authorization headers with Zoho OAuth tokens. Search results also reference API keys in the MindCloud wrapper integration.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for Zoho Cliq and create applications in the Zoho Developer Console to obtain OAuth credentials. Zoho Cliq offers a free plan after trial expiration.
api_breadth_detail: Developer platform supports integrations, bots, commands, message actions, functions, and access to available endpoints for automation and embedding Cliq into external systems.
mcp_server_detail: Zoho offers Zoho MCP, an MCP infrastructure/service for exposing Zoho app tools and actions to AI agents via the Model Context Protocol. The search results do not explicitly confirm a dedicated Zoho Cliq MCP server, but Zoho MCP supports Zoho services broadly. https://www.zoho.com/mcp/services/zoho-services.html
buildability_detail: Zoho Cliq has public developer documentation, REST APIs, OAuth2 authentication, and self-serve developer onboarding through Zoho accounts and developer console. MCP support exists at the Zoho ecosystem level.

one_line_description: Enterprise collaboration platform with messaging, docs, calendar, video conferencing, and workflow APIs.
auth_details: Lark apps use app credentials (app ID and app secret) to obtain app_access_token and tenant_access_token, and also supports user_access_token for calling APIs as a user. Documentation includes app authentication and authorization flows.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create apps directly through the Lark Developer Console using the publicly accessible 'CREATE APP' flow. API docs and developer console are publicly available. Some advanced APIs may require paid quota packages, but core API access is available self-serve.
api_breadth_detail: Extensive server-side REST APIs covering contacts, messaging, docs, Base, sheets, wiki, approvals, calendar, video conferencing, bots, authentication, event subscriptions, and more. The API list indicates broad platform coverage across core collaboration features.
mcp_server_detail: Official MCP server exists: 'larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp' on GitHub. It exposes Feishu/Lark Open Platform APIs as MCP tools for AI agents and supports document processing, messaging, calendar scheduling, and more. Also listed on mcp.so.
buildability_detail: Lark provides a public developer platform with self-serve app creation, broad REST APIs, token-based authentication flows, and official MCP tooling. Composio could build an agent toolkit today using the documented APIs.

one_line_description: Team communication and messaging platform with chat, voice/video meetings, and integrations.
auth_details: Search results indicate Pumble apps can act on behalf of authorized users or bots, implying OAuth-style authorization via app installs. Official MCP setup requires a user/bot token and x-app-token (App key) passed in headers. MindCloud wrapper docs also reference Bearer token authentication using an API key.
self_serve_detail: Pumble offers a free plan ('Start using Pumble for free'). MCP instructions state developers can create a Pumble addon/app and obtain credentials themselves.
api_breadth_detail: Evidence references a Pumble REST API and MCP exposure of 26 tools covering channels, messages, scheduled messages, and users. Coverage appears to include core messaging/workspace functionality but full endpoint breadth is unclear from results.
mcp_server_detail: Official Pumble MCP server documented by Pumble Help Center at https://mcp.pumble.com/mcp. Supports Claude, Gemini, Codex, and CLI integrations using app keys and user/bot tokens. Community listing also exists on MCP Market describing 26 strongly-typed tools over the Pumble REST API.
buildability_detail: Pumble appears to provide a public REST API with self-serve app/addon creation and standard token/app-key authentication. Official MCP server further simplifies agent integration.

one_line_description: Communication platform with messaging, voice, communities, and bot/app integrations.
auth_details: Discord supports OAuth2 authorization code, implicit, client credentials, and Discord-specific bot/webhook flows. Bot applications authenticate using bot tokens; user access uses OAuth2 bearer tokens.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-register applications through the Discord Developer Portal and obtain client IDs, client secrets, and bot tokens without sales contact. Some scopes are restricted to approved partners.
api_breadth_detail: Discord provides extensive developer APIs covering messages, channels, guilds/servers, users, webhooks, commands, permissions, stickers, emojis, threads, moderation, scheduled events, and more via a large public API reference.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist for Discord, including 'discord-mcp' (https://mcpservers.org/servers/exilproductions/discord-mcp) with broad server/channel/message management support, and GitHub projects such as https://github.com/v-3/discordmcp.
buildability_detail: Discord has a mature public developer platform with self-serve application registration, standard OAuth2 and bot token authentication, and broad REST API coverage suitable for building agent toolkits today.

one_line_description: Cloud-based messaging platform with APIs for bots and client applications.
auth_details: Telegram Bot API uses bot token–based authentication obtained from BotFather. Telegram client APIs also use phone-number/SMS code based user authorization with optional 2FA as described in MTProto auth flow.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create Telegram bots and obtain bot tokens themselves via BotFather. Telegram Bot API is described as completely free with unlimited bots/messages in referenced pricing guides.
api_breadth_detail: Telegram provides broad messaging platform capabilities through the Bot API and Telegram APIs, including messaging, channels, bots, authentication, and client interactions.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist for Telegram, including BrainDAO/mcp-telegram on GitHub for interacting with Telegram bots/channels and MCP Telegram implementations listed on MCP directories. Example: https://github.com/IQAIcom/mcp-telegram
buildability_detail: Telegram exposes public APIs with self-serve developer onboarding and standard token-based bot authentication. Community MCP servers already exist, indicating straightforward integration potential for Composio.

one_line_description: Business messaging platform and APIs from Meta for sending and managing WhatsApp communications.
auth_details: Meta WhatsApp Cloud API uses secure access tokens generated through the Meta developer platform and connected Meta apps/WhatsApp Business accounts. Authentication and authorization are documented as part of the platform setup.
self_serve_detail: Developers can register as Meta developers, create a Meta app, connect or create a WhatsApp Business account, access test numbers, sandbox resources, and start building without sales approval. Pricing is usage-based.
api_breadth_detail: The WhatsApp Business Platform exposes Cloud API, Business Management API, marketing messaging APIs, webhooks, message templates, media handling, account management, and messaging operations across many endpoints using HTTP requests.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for WhatsApp/WhatsApp Business API integrations, including 'WhatsApp Business API MCP Server' (https://mcp.so/server/Whatsapp-MCP-Server/mattcoatsworth) and GitHub project https://github.com/lharries/whatsapp-mcp.
buildability_detail: WhatsApp Business provides a public REST API with self-serve developer onboarding, documented authentication using Meta access tokens, test resources, and broad messaging capabilities. Composio could build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Cloud-based business phone and call center platform with APIs and webhooks for integrations.
auth_details: Aircall Public API supports Basic Authentication using an Authorization header with Base64 encoded api_id:api_token credentials. Aircall also supports OAuth flow for integrations, returning an access_token used to authenticate API requests.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access public API documentation and create integrations. Search results indicate API access is included in paid plans; no evidence of partnership approval required. Pricing appears self-serve for Essentials/Professional plans, though enterprise features may require sales contact.
api_breadth_detail: Aircall provides a REST Public API and webhooks for integrating with accounts, calls, CRM systems, and event notifications. Documentation references authentication, rate limiting, pagination, and multiple tutorials, suggesting coverage of core telephony and integration features.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for Aircall was found in the provided search results.
buildability_detail: Aircall exposes a public REST API with standard authentication methods (Basic Auth and OAuth), public developer documentation, and webhook support. Developers appear able to obtain access through standard product signup flows without partnership gating.

one_line_description: Communications APIs for SMS, voice, video, messaging, and verification.
auth_details: Verify API supports Basic authentication using API Key and API Secret Base64-encoded in the Authorization header, and JWT Bearer authentication using Application ID and Private Key. CAMARA APIs additionally support OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow with Bearer tokens.
self_serve_detail: Vonage Developer Center advertises developers can 'Try it free' and access documentation directly via the developer portal.
api_breadth_detail: Public APIs cover SMS, Voice, Messages, Verify, Video, RTC, and Contact Center functionality with extensive documentation and SDKs.
mcp_server_detail: Official Vonage MCP Server exists with documentation and technical details. Covers Vonage APIs for Voice, Messaging, Video, and documentation search via the Model Context Protocol. Docs: https://developer.vonage.com/en/mcp-server/overview
buildability_detail: Vonage provides public REST APIs, self-serve developer onboarding with free trial access, standard authentication methods (Basic, JWT, OAuth2), and official MCP server support, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit.

one_line_description: Programmatic API for managing Google Ads accounts, campaigns, reporting, and bidding.
auth_details: Google Ads API uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication and authorization. Access also requires a Google Ads developer token obtained from the API Center of a Google Ads manager account.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a Google Ads manager account (MCC) and apply for a developer token through the API Center. Tokens have access levels (Test, Basic, Standard). No explicit sales gate mentioned, though an application form is required.
api_breadth_detail: The API supports automated account management, campaign management, reporting, inventory-based ad management, Smart Bidding strategy management, and other core Google Ads operations across accounts and campaigns.
mcp_server_detail: Official Google Ads MCP server exists from Google Ads developers. Docs available at https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/developer-toolkit/mcp-server and source referenced at https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp. The MCP server enables natural-language access to campaign data and management capabilities.
buildability_detail: Google Ads provides a public API with OAuth2 authentication, developer self-service onboarding via MCC accounts and developer tokens, broad API coverage, and an official MCP server. Some onboarding friction exists because developers must apply for a developer token, but this does not appear to require sales involvement.

one_line_description: Advertising and marketing API platform for managing Meta/Facebook/Instagram ad campaigns, creatives, targeting, and reporting.
auth_details: Uses Meta access tokens for authentication, including user access tokens, long-lived tokens, and system user access tokens obtained through Meta apps and Graph API Explorer.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a Meta Developer account and app to obtain development access and generate access tokens. Production-scale access may require App Review and business verification.
api_breadth_detail: The Marketing API/Graph API covers campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, insights/reporting, targeting, media, Pages, catalogs, commerce, and related ad management workflows across Meta properties.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP server exists: 'Meta Ads MCP Server' covering 54 tools for campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, insights, targeting, Pages, and more via Meta Graph API v22.0. Additional reports mention an official Meta Ads MCP released in 2026.
buildability_detail: Meta Ads provides a public Marketing API with self-serve developer onboarding and token-based authentication. There are some production caveats such as App Review, business verification, and rate limits for higher access tiers, but Composio could build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: LinkedIn's advertising and marketing platform API for managing ad accounts, campaigns, creatives, and reporting.
auth_details: LinkedIn APIs use OAuth 2.0 for user authorization and API authentication. Marketing/Advertising API access requires approved permissions. API requests use Bearer access tokens in the Authorization header.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create an app and apply for Advertising API Development tier access through the Developer Portal, but advertising permissions require LinkedIn approval. Not fully self-serve because marketing integrations must be approved.
api_breadth_detail: Marketing/Advertising REST APIs cover ad accounts, campaigns, account users, creatives, and related marketing operations. Access tiers support reading and editing multiple ad accounts and creating accounts via API.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist for LinkedIn Ads, including https://github.com/radiateb2b/mcp-linkedinads and listings on LobeHub and MCPServers.org. These servers allow AI assistants to analyze LinkedIn Ads data using LinkedIn access tokens.
buildability_blocker: Advertising API access requires LinkedIn approval
buildability_detail: LinkedIn Ads has a public REST API with OAuth2 authentication and broad marketing coverage, but developers must apply for and receive approval for Advertising API access tiers before using production capabilities.

one_line_description: CRM and marketing automation platform with APIs for contacts, messaging, calendars, sales, payments, and workflows.
auth_details: HighLevel API documentation references OAuth-based integrations and private integration tokens (PIT). Search results describe OAuth 2.0 for marketplace/public integrations and Private Integration Tokens for internal tools/MCP access.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign in to the developer portal and create marketplace apps or private integrations. API access appears tied to paid plans/trials; search results mention a 14-day free trial and API access included on qualifying plans, though some community discussion suggests lower-tier plans may not include API access.
api_breadth_detail: Comprehensive REST API covering contacts, conversations/messaging, calendars, opportunities/sales pipelines, payments, webhooks, workflows, and more across the CRM platform.
mcp_server_detail: Official HighLevel MCP server documented by HighLevel. Supports querying and automating HighLevel data/tools via MCP clients using Private Integration Tokens. Docs: https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/other/mcp . Additional setup guide: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007981-highlevel-mcp-server-connect-ai-agents-to-highlevel-tools
buildability_detail: GoHighLevel provides a public REST API with OAuth2 and token-based authentication, broad platform coverage, developer documentation, webhook support, and an official MCP server. Access may require a paid plan, but developers can self-serve through the developer portal and trials.

one_line_description: Email marketing and marketing automation platform with APIs for campaigns, audiences, analytics, and more.
auth_details: Mailchimp Marketing API supports OAuth 2 for accessing data on behalf of other users and API keys for direct account access. Documentation also references Basic Auth using username:apikey or username:access_token.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a Mailchimp account and generate API keys directly from the developer portal/docs without sales approval. Search results also reference a free plan/free trial availability.
api_breadth_detail: The Mailchimp Marketing API provides broad coverage across campaigns, audiences, contact data, analytics, automations, templates, reports, e-commerce, landing pages, and related marketing resources.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Mailchimp, including an open-source GitHub project (damientilman/mailchimp-mcp-server) covering campaigns, audiences, members, automations, reporting, e-commerce, landing pages, surveys, and more. Also listed on Apify and LobeHub.
buildability_detail: Mailchimp exposes a public REST API with standard OAuth2/API key authentication and self-serve developer onboarding, making it suitable for building an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Marketing automation and customer engagement platform for email, SMS, and CRM workflows.
auth_details: Klaviyo supports three authentication methods: private API keys for server-side /api endpoints, OAuth for server-side APIs, and public API keys for client-side /client endpoints. Private API keys are passed in the Authorization header as 'Klaviyo-API-Key your-private-api-key'.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a Klaviyo account on the free plan and obtain API credentials through the developer setup flow. Klaviyo offers a free tier with up to 250 active profiles and 500 email sends per month.
api_breadth_detail: Klaviyo provides extensive REST APIs covering profiles, lists, segments, campaigns, flows, events, back-in-stock features, tracking, and more. Documentation references OpenAPI specs and Postman collections for current APIs plus legacy v1/v2 APIs.
mcp_server_detail: Both community and official MCP servers exist. A public GitHub project (https://github.com/mattcoatsworth/Klaviyo-MCP-Server) provides broad API coverage for profiles, lists, segments, campaigns, and flows. Klaviyo also announced an official MCP server available to customers in 2025: https://investors.klaviyo.com/news/news-details/2025/Klaviyo-MCP-server-helps-marketers-move-faster-with-AI-2025-twExpbyTVx/default.aspx
buildability_detail: Klaviyo has a public REST API with standard authentication methods (OAuth2 and API keys), self-serve developer onboarding via a free plan, comprehensive API documentation, and existing MCP ecosystem support.

one_line_description: All-in-one marketing platform for funnels, email marketing, courses, automations, and online business management.
auth_details: Public REST API authenticates via API keys, including X-API-Key header tokens generated in account settings. MCP keys are also generated in the settings area. YouTube tutorial mentions OAuth support is planned in the future but not currently available.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for a free plan and generate API/MCP keys themselves from account settings without sales approval. Search results indicate API access is available on free plan for core endpoints and included with paid plans.
api_breadth_detail: Public REST API covers contacts, tags, custom fields, funnels, sales, subscription operations, newsletter management, and indirect automation triggers. Documentation describes a selected subset of platform functionality rather than full product coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Official systeme.io MCP server exists. Documentation states it supports contact management (contacts, tags, custom fields), newsletter management, and funnels. Integration guides are available for ChatGPT and Claude. Evidence: https://help.systeme.io/article/9489-how-to-use-systeme-ios-mcp
buildability_detail: Systeme.io provides a public REST API with self-serve API key authentication and free-plan access, plus an official MCP server. Standard auth and publicly documented endpoints make it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Social media and visual discovery platform with APIs for content, ads, shopping, and analytics management.
auth_details: Pinterest API uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code grant with app ID, client secret, redirect URI, scopes, and access tokens for user-authorized API access.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create apps and obtain Trial API access through the Pinterest Developer Platform. Trial and Standard access tiers are described as free, though Standard access may require approval/review.
api_breadth_detail: Pinterest REST API v5 covers content management (pins/boards), ad management, targeting, shopping/catalogs, analytics/reporting, audiences, campaigns, and more across many endpoints.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Pinterest API integration, including https://github.com/collactivelabs/pinterest-mcp-server and a LobeHub-listed Pinterest MCP server for pins, boards, and analytics. No official public Pinterest MCP server was found.
buildability_blocker: API access approval tiers and rate limits
buildability_detail: Pinterest provides a public REST API with OAuth2 authentication and self-serve developer onboarding via trial access. However, production-scale or broader access may require approval for Standard access and is subject to rate limits and platform review.

one_line_description: Meta’s Threads API enables developers to publish posts, manage conversations, and retrieve analytics/content from Threads accounts.
auth_details: Threads API uses Meta authorization flows where users grant permissions through an Authorization Window and the app exchanges an authorization code for short-lived Threads user access tokens; tokens can be short-lived or long-lived.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a Meta app, select the Threads use case, and obtain API access through the Meta developer portal. The API is described as publicly available and free to use, though production use for non-role users requires App Review approval and app publishing.
api_breadth_detail: The Threads API provides endpoints for publishing posts, replies, retrieving media, analytics, and managing Threads presence. Documentation includes overview, guides, and endpoint references at graph.threads.net.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Threads integrations, including ThreadsMcpNet (.NET MCP server for content creation on Threads) and a TypeScript-based threads-mcp server. There is also a broader Meta Platform MCP server covering Instagram Graph API and Threads API. Sources: https://medium.com/@tttndev13/a-mcp-server-for-content-creation-on-threads-7cb26cc784ca , https://mcp.aibase.com/server/1916354827725545473 , https://mcpmarket.com/server/meta-platform
buildability_detail: Threads has a public developer platform with REST APIs, OAuth-based authentication, self-serve app creation, and published API references. Some production permissions require Meta App Review before broad user access, but Composio could build an integration today.

one_line_description: Cloud email delivery and marketing email platform for transactional and campaign messaging.
auth_details: Twilio SendGrid supports API keys passed as Bearer tokens in the Authorization header for API access. Some services also support Basic authentication using an API key as the password value.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for a free tier/free trial and generate SendGrid API keys themselves. Search results indicate a free offering of 100 emails/day without requiring a credit card.
api_breadth_detail: SendGrid exposes broad REST APIs covering email sending, marketing campaigns, domain authentication, templates, reporting, and related email infrastructure features. Search results reference OpenAPI specs and multiple endpoint groups under /v3.
mcp_server_detail: Community and tutorial MCP servers exist for SendGrid. Examples include the open-source GitHub project 'sendgrid-mcp' and Twilio's blog tutorial for building a SendGrid MCP server for AI email workflows. URLs: https://github.com/garethcull/sendgrid-mcp and https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/community/build-a-sendgrid-mcp-server-for-ai-email-workflows
buildability_detail: SendGrid has a public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding with free usage, standard API key authentication, and existing MCP ecosystem examples, making it straightforward for Composio to build an agent toolkit.

one_line_description: Ecommerce platform with APIs for storefronts, admin operations, customers, orders, inventory, and app integrations.
auth_details: Shopify supports OAuth-based authentication and authorization flows for apps, including authorization code grant and token exchange. Storefront API uses access tokens passed in the X-Shopify-Storefront-Access-Token header.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-serve via Shopify developer tooling and development stores. API access is available with a Shopify store subscription, and partners can create development stores for free testing.
api_breadth_detail: Shopify provides extensive Admin, Storefront, Customer Account, and Partner APIs covering products, orders, customers, inventory, apps, storefronts, and more across a large API surface.
mcp_server_detail: Both official/community MCP servers exist. Shopify/dev-mcp provides MCP access to Shopify APIs and docs; community project antoineschaller/shopify-mcp-server integrates with Shopify Admin API and exposes tools for products, orders, customers, inventory, and analytics. Sources: https://www.augmentcode.com/mcp/shopify-dev-mcp and https://github.com/antoineschaller/shopify-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Shopify has mature public REST and GraphQL APIs, self-serve developer onboarding, standard OAuth authentication, and broad API coverage suitable for building agent toolkits today.

one_line_description: Open-source ecommerce platform for WordPress with REST APIs for store management and storefront operations.
auth_details: WooCommerce REST API supports pre-generated REST API keys created in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API. It also states authentication can use any WordPress REST API authentication plugin or method. Deprecated MCP endpoint authenticates using WooCommerce REST API keys in the X-MCP-API-Key header.
self_serve_detail: WooCommerce core plugin is free and open source, and developers can generate their own REST API keys from the WordPress/WooCommerce admin dashboard without partnership approval.
api_breadth_detail: WooCommerce provides a REST API integrated with the WordPress REST API (v3) supporting create/read/update/delete operations for store data including orders, products, customers, carts, checkout, shipping, taxes, discounts, and more. Store API also exposes customer-facing commerce endpoints.
mcp_server_detail: WooCommerce has official MCP integration documentation at https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/features/mcp describing native MCP support and a deprecated MCP endpoint. Community MCP servers also exist, including https://github.com/techspawn/woocommerce-mcp-server and StackOne's hosted MCP connector.
buildability_detail: WooCommerce exposes a public REST API with self-serve API key generation and extensive coverage of ecommerce resources. Authentication is straightforward and MCP support exists officially and via community implementations, making agent toolkit development feasible today.

one_line_description: Ecommerce platform with APIs for store management, storefronts, customers, carts, orders, and headless commerce integrations.
auth_details: BigCommerce documents OAuth-based API accounts including store-level, app-level, and account-level credentials for REST APIs. B2B Edition docs reference use of BigCommerce API authentication tokens via the X-Auth-Token header together with X-Store-Hash for server-to-server requests.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create API accounts and credentials through the BigCommerce control panel/developer platform without requiring partnership approval according to the API Accounts documentation.
api_breadth_detail: BigCommerce provides multiple APIs including REST Storefront API, GraphQL Storefront API, Customer Login API, Current Customer API, and management APIs covering products, customers, carts, checkouts, orders, authentication, and headless commerce workflows.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for BigCommerce, including 'bigcommerce-api-mcp' on GitHub and listings on MCP Market and LobeHub. These servers expose BigCommerce REST API operations for products, customers, and orders. URLs: https://github.com/isaacgounton/bigcommerce-api-mcp and https://mcpmarket.com/server/bigcommerce
buildability_detail: BigCommerce offers public REST and GraphQL APIs with documented OAuth authentication and self-serve API account creation, making it suitable for building an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Enterprise ecommerce platform with APIs for B2C/B2B commerce, pricing, promotions, products, carts, and storefront integrations.
auth_details: SCAPI Admin APIs and Shopper APIs use access tokens in the form of JSON Web Tokens (JWT) sent via Bearer authentication headers. Admin APIs use OAuth2 access tokens obtained from Account Manager via oauth2/access_token. Shopper APIs require creating a SLAS client and calling the /token endpoint.
self_serve_detail: Developer documentation is public, but practical access to Salesforce Commerce Cloud environments and sandboxes appears gated. Trailblazer community responses indicate free developer sandbox access is generally unavailable unless you are an ISV partner.
api_breadth_detail: Commerce APIs cover products, pricing, promotions, carts, checkout, shopper APIs, admin APIs, and custom APIs across B2C/B2B commerce use cases. Documentation references numerous REST resources and endpoints.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP server exists: 'Commerce Cloud MCP Server' on mcpservers.org connects AI applications to Salesforce Commerce Cloud via MCP using OCAPI access. Additional Salesforce-related MCP server projects also exist on GitHub. No official Commerce Cloud MCP server confirmed.
buildability_blocker: Access to Commerce Cloud environments and API credentials may require partnership or paid enterprise access.
buildability_detail: Salesforce Commerce Cloud exposes broad public REST APIs with standard OAuth2/JWT bearer authentication, making toolkit development technically feasible. However, developer self-serve access appears limited and sandbox/API access may require enterprise accounts or partner status.

one_line_description: Ecommerce platform providing REST and GraphQL APIs for products, orders, customers, carts, inventory, and store management.
auth_details: Search results indicate Adobe Commerce APIs support OAuth 1.0a and token-based Bearer authentication against merchant-hosted instances.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access Adobe Commerce developer resources and Marketplace developer portal documentation self-serve. Magento Open Source is publicly available, though Adobe Commerce enterprise editions are paid.
api_breadth_detail: Comprehensive REST and GraphQL APIs covering products, categories, customers, carts, checkout, orders, inventory, CMS content, pricing, and store configuration with extensive endpoint references.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Magento/Adobe Commerce, including Magento Adobe Commerce MCP Server and Magento MCP Server with 30+ admin tools for catalog management, promotions, CMS, and diagnostics. Sources: https://mcpmarket.com/server/magento-adobe-commerce and https://lobehub.com/mcp/thomastx05-magento-mcp
buildability_detail: Adobe Commerce exposes broad public REST and GraphQL APIs with standard authentication methods and publicly accessible developer documentation. Community MCP servers further demonstrate agent integration feasibility.

one_line_description: Website builder and ecommerce platform with commerce APIs for managing merchant sites, products, orders, inventory, analytics, and contacts.
auth_details: Squarespace Commerce APIs require authenticated requests. Commercial integrations use OAuth 2.0 credentials and authorization flows. Custom applications for a merchant site are available on Commerce Advanced plans; search results and third-party docs reference developer API keys for site-level access.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access Commerce APIs through a Squarespace merchant subscription, particularly Commerce Advanced plans for custom applications. API access appears bundled with site subscriptions rather than requiring partnership approval.
api_breadth_detail: Commerce APIs cover many major commerce resources including contacts, analytics, products, websites, inventory, orders, transactions, profiles, and webhook subscriptions. Docs describe APIs as REST-based over HTTPS.
mcp_server_detail: A community MCP server exists on GitHub: https://github.com/BusyBee3333/squarespace-mcp-2026-complete . It claims broad Squarespace API coverage with 67+ tools and OAuth2 support. No official Squarespace MCP server was found in the provided results.
buildability_blocker: API access tied to paid Squarespace commerce plans; some APIs noted as maintenance mode.
buildability_detail: Squarespace provides public REST Commerce APIs with OAuth2 authentication and broad ecommerce coverage, making toolkit development feasible today. However, API access is bundled with merchant subscriptions (not a standalone free developer tier), and some APIs are in maintenance mode with guidance to use newer Contacts APIs.

one_line_description: E-commerce platform with APIs for managing stores, products, orders, storefronts, and apps.
auth_details: Ecwid REST API uses OAuth 2.0 for public apps. For custom single-store apps, developers can obtain access tokens directly from the app dashboard and use them as Bearer tokens. Apps also have client_id and client_secret API keys.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up and start building via the Ecwid developer portal. Ecwid creates a custom app for users visiting the app dashboard for the first time, enabling API access without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: REST API covers store data, payment and shipping methods, storefront settings, orders, products, and app integrations. Documentation indicates broad store management coverage.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for Ecwid was found in the provided search results.
buildability_detail: Ecwid provides a public REST API with OAuth2/token authentication and self-serve developer onboarding through its developer portal and custom app system, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Ecommerce platform for creators to sell digital products and memberships.
auth_details: Gumroad API supports OAuth-based application authentication with Application ID/Secret and redirect URI setup. Access tokens/seller tokens can also be used directly via environment variable or API access token.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a Gumroad application themselves to generate API credentials and access tokens. Public Postman workspace also indicates free signup access.
api_breadth_detail: REST API covering products, sales, subscribers, license verification, offer codes, and related creator commerce functionality. Evidence suggests multiple core ecommerce endpoints but not necessarily full platform coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Gumroad API integration, including open-source Gumroad MCP Server implementations listed on MCP marketplaces and GitHub integrations. Examples: https://mcp.so/server/gumroad-mcp/rmarescu and https://lobehub.com/pl/mcp/rmarescu-gumroad-mcp
buildability_detail: Gumroad provides a public REST API with OAuth2/access token authentication and self-serve developer setup, making it feasible for Composio to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: REST-based API for Amazon sellers and vendors to access orders, inventory, shipments, payments, reports, and other marketplace operations.
auth_details: Uses Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth2 flows to obtain access and refresh tokens for seller-authorized access; restricted operations use Restricted Access Tokens (RDTs). Requests are also signed with AWS credentials (AWS access key ID and secret access key) via AWS signing mechanisms.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-register by creating a Professional selling account and submitting a developer profile in Developer Central. No partnership approval explicitly required, but a Professional seller account is mandatory. Historically free access; fees announced starting in 2026.
api_breadth_detail: SP-API covers orders, shipments, payments, inventory, listings, returns, reports, and other seller/vendor workflows across Amazon marketplaces with extensive endpoint coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Amazon Selling Partner API, including https://github.com/jay-trivedi/amazon_sp_mcp and additional SP-API MCP implementations listed on MCP directories such as LobeHub and MCP Market.
buildability_blocker: Developer onboarding requires a Professional selling account and seller authorization.
buildability_detail: Amazon provides a public REST API with standard OAuth2-style authorization and broad coverage, making toolkit development feasible today. However, developers must maintain a Professional seller account, register as an SP-API developer, and obtain seller authorization for many workflows.

one_line_description: Payments and subscription platform for creators and businesses with APIs for checkout, transactions, subscriptions, and webhooks.
auth_details: Search results reference API-key based authentication via headers in API requests. The FanBasis docs themselves are login-gated, while related API docs describe custom integrations and payment workflows.
self_serve_detail: Public API reference exists, but the developer docs at dev-docs.fanbasis.com require a password/login. No evidence in the search results of open self-serve developer signup or instant API credential issuance.
api_breadth_detail: API reference mentions payment links/checkout sessions, transactions, subscriptions, customer rewards, and webhooks for automation. Coverage appears focused on payments and subscription workflows.
mcp_server_detail: No evidence of an official or community MCP server for FanBasis in the provided search results.
buildability_blocker: Developer access appears gated behind login/password-protected docs.
buildability_detail: FanBasis appears to expose a public REST-style API for payments, subscriptions, transactions, and webhooks, which is sufficient for an agent toolkit. However, self-serve developer onboarding and authentication details are unclear because the primary developer docs are password protected.

one_line_description: SEO data platform offering APIs for SERP results, keywords, backlinks, on-page audits, domain analytics, and competitor research.
auth_details: DataForSEO API v3 uses HTTP Basic Authentication with login and password credentials encoded in the Authorization header; credentials are obtained from the DataForSEO API access portal.
self_serve_detail: Developers can obtain API credentials through the DataForSEO app/API access portal and use pay-as-you-go billing. Search results indicate a $50 minimum deposit and removal of previous monthly commitment requirements for some APIs, suggesting self-serve onboarding without partnership approval.
api_breadth_detail: Broad REST API coverage including SERP results, keyword data, backlinks, DataForSEO Labs analytics, merchant/product data, on-page audits, domain analytics, competitor research, and AI optimization data across many endpoints.
mcp_server_detail: Official DataForSEO MCP server announced by DataForSEO for connecting AI models to SEO data: https://dataforseo.com/blog/dataforseo-mcp-server-bridging-the-gap-between-ai-models-and-seo-data . Community MCP implementation also exists at https://github.com/Skobyn/dataforseo-mcp-server and directory listing at https://mcp.so/server/mcp-server-typescript/dataforseo
buildability_detail: DataForSEO provides a public REST API with standard HTTP Basic authentication, broad endpoint coverage, documented authentication, and self-serve API access via pay-as-you-go onboarding, making it suitable for building an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: SEO platform providing APIs for keyword, backlink, domain, audit, AI search, and project data.
auth_details: All requests to the Data API must be authenticated using a generated API key from the SE Ranking account dashboard. A single API key works across both the Data API and Project API.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for a 14-day trial with full API and MCP access from day one. API keys are self-generated from the dashboard. Paid plans and pay-as-you-go API credits are also available without requiring partnership approval.
api_breadth_detail: SE Ranking exposes Data API and Project API endpoints covering keywords, backlinks, domains, audits, AI search/GEO data, projects, tracked keywords, and related SEO workflows. Documentation references multiple endpoint groups and broad SEO data access.
mcp_server_detail: SE Ranking provides an official MCP Server at https://api.seranking.com/mcp with integrations for Claude, Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT, and other MCP-compatible clients. It exposes live SEO and GEO data through the API.
buildability_detail: SE Ranking has a public REST API authenticated with self-serve API keys, a free trial with immediate API access, broad SEO data coverage, and an official MCP server, making it suitable for building an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: SEO and marketing intelligence platform offering APIs for keywords, backlinks, rankings, and AI search visibility data.
auth_details: Direct Ahrefs API requests require an API key. Ahrefs Connect developers can test OAuth flows for integrations before app approval/activation.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access docs publicly and use limited free test queries on non-eligible plans. Full API access is available on eligible paid plans; Ahrefs Connect apps start in inactive mode and require approval for activation.
api_breadth_detail: REST API v3 covers keyword research, backlink analysis, rank tracking, brand visibility, management/public endpoints, and broader Ahrefs workspace data with many endpoints/resources.
mcp_server_detail: Ahrefs provides an official hosted MCP server for MCP-compatible AI tools. Endpoint referenced as https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp. Docs: https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/mcp/docs/introduction
buildability_blocker: Full API access tied to eligible paid plans and some integration flows may require app approval.
buildability_detail: Ahrefs has a public REST API, API keys, developer documentation, and an official MCP server. However, meaningful production access appears restricted to eligible paid plans, and Ahrefs Connect apps require approval before activation.

one_line_description: AI-powered web scraping platform with APIs to run scrapers and retrieve scraping analytics/results.
auth_details: MrScraper API uses API token authentication. Requests include the token in the x-api-token header; some analytics endpoints use the token as a query parameter.
self_serve_detail: Documentation references contacting support to request an API token for endpoints on other hosts. Search results do not clearly show a public self-serve developer signup or free trial for direct API access.
api_breadth_detail: REST API supports running scrapers, retrieving scraping results, and analytics endpoints. Documentation shows scraper execution, multi-page scraping, streaming responses, and results retrieval endpoints.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for MrScraper was found in the provided search results.
buildability_blocker: Unclear self-serve developer onboarding/API credential access
buildability_detail: MrScraper exposes a documented REST API with standard API token authentication, so integration is technically feasible. However, available evidence suggests API token access may require contacting support for some endpoints, and no clear self-serve developer onboarding/free tier documentation was found.

one_line_description: Platform for web scraping, data extraction, and automation using Actors and APIs.
auth_details: Apify API v2 uses API tokens passed via the Authorization header as a Bearer token (recommended) or as a URL query parameter.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-sign up for a permanent free plan with $5 monthly credits and no credit card required according to pricing/free-tier information.
api_breadth_detail: Apify provides a REST API v2 covering Actors, runs, datasets, key-value stores, webhooks, user endpoints, and platform automation. Documentation references a downloadable OpenAPI schema and multiple resource endpoints.
mcp_server_detail: An official/community MCP server repository exists: 'actors-mcp-server' by Apify for running Apify Actors through the Model Context Protocol. Apify also has an MCP servers category in its store.
buildability_detail: Apify has a public REST API with token authentication, extensive API coverage, public documentation, downloadable OpenAPI schema, and self-serve developer onboarding with a free plan.

one_line_description: AI-focused web scraping, crawling, search, and extraction API for agent-ready web data.
auth_details: API uses Bearer authentication with a Firecrawl API key in the Authorization header (e.g. 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY'). SDKs also initialize with an apiKey parameter.
self_serve_detail: Developers can start for free and obtain API keys through the Firecrawl dashboard. Pricing page explicitly says 'Start for free, then scale as you grow.' Search results also mention a free tier for testing search, crawling, and extraction capabilities.
api_breadth_detail: REST API covers scraping, crawling, website mapping, web search, extraction, monitoring, and interaction workflows. Documentation references multiple resources/endpoints including scrape, crawl, map, search, extract, and monitor capabilities.
mcp_server_detail: Official MCP server exists via GitHub and npm package 'firecrawl-mcp'. Supports search, scrape, crawl, extract, interact, and monitor capabilities. Hosted endpoint available at https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp with optional keyless free tier for some tools. Sources: https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server and https://www.npmjs.com/package/firecrawl-mcp
buildability_detail: Firecrawl provides a public REST API with self-serve signup/free tier, standard API key bearer authentication, SDKs, and extensive scraping/search endpoints. Official MCP support further simplifies agent integrations.

one_line_description: Web data platform for large-scale web scraping, proxy infrastructure, SERP APIs, and AI agent web access.
auth_details: Bright Data supports API access using an API key/token and native proxy access using username and password credentials. API requests require an API key; proxy/native access uses proxy username and password.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a new Bright Data account and receive 5,000 free credits per month automatically across eligible APIs and scraping products. API keys can be generated from the control panel account settings.
api_breadth_detail: Bright Data provides multiple APIs and scraping services including Web Unlocker API, SERP API, Web Scraper API, search, crawling, scraping, browser automation, and structured data extraction across many site types.
mcp_server_detail: Bright Data offers an official MCP server called 'The Web MCP' with free tier support for AI agents. It supports web search, scraping as Markdown, structured data extraction, browser automation, and hosted/local deployment options. Sources: https://brightdata.com/ai/mcp-server and https://brightdata.com/pricing/mcp-server
buildability_detail: Bright Data exposes public APIs with self-serve signup, free credits, standard API key authentication, and official MCP support. Composio could build an agent toolkit today using the publicly documented APIs and MCP offerings.

one_line_description: Open-source OSINT tool for searching usernames across social networks and websites.
auth_details: CloudFerro Sherlock documentation states the service uses API keys for authentication, created within a project in the Control Panel.
self_serve_detail: The Sherlock project and API repository are publicly accessible on GitHub, suggesting developers can self-serve access to the open-source code and API components without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: Public GitHub repository exposes an API service and CLI components for Sherlock functionality. Coverage appears focused on username/account search and related OSINT operations rather than a large enterprise platform.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP server exists: Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp provides FastMCP integration for Sherlock OSINT username searches across 400+ platforms. https://github.com/Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp
