buildability_blocker: API details and hosting/authentication model are somewhat fragmented between open-source and hosted variants.
buildability_detail: An agent toolkit could likely be built today using the open-source Sherlock API/MCP integrations, but the available search results do not clearly document a standardized hosted public API surface or developer onboarding flow for the core Sherlock project.

one_line_description: Contact and company intelligence enrichment API aggregating multiple data vendors for prospecting and GTM workflows.
auth_details: All requests require an API key sent in the `x-api-key` header. Base URL documented as `https://api.waterfall.io/v1/`.
self_serve_detail: Public docs exist, but website messaging says 'Talk to our team' and no evidence of open self-serve signup, free tier, or instant API key issuance was found in the provided results.
api_breadth_detail: REST API covers contact prospecting, contact search, contact enrichment, phone enrichment, company enrichment, and company title lookup endpoints. Documentation suggests several core GTM/data enrichment resources with async and sync operations.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for Waterfall.io was found in the provided search results.
buildability_blocker: Likely sales-gated or non-self-serve API access
buildability_detail: Waterfall.io has a documented public REST API using standard API key authentication, making technical integration straightforward. However, the available evidence suggests access may require contacting the company rather than immediate self-serve developer onboarding.

one_line_description: AI-powered go-to-market data enrichment and workflow automation platform with integrations and HTTP API capabilities.
auth_details: Clay's HTTP API integration supports standard API authentication patterns. Docs mention saving API keys or bearer tokens in HTTP API Headers accounts, and a separate HTTP API with JWT Authentication action for dynamically issued tokens.
self_serve_detail: Clay offers self-serve pricing plans and signup via clay.com pricing page. However, community reports indicate HTTP API access may require higher-tier paid plans ($300-$495+/month).
api_breadth_detail: Publicly documented HTTP API integration supports GET, POST, PUT, DELETE requests to external APIs and databases. Search results do not expose a full public developer API reference for all Clay resources, suggesting moderate or unclear direct platform API coverage.
mcp_server_detail: Clay has an official MCP offering described at https://www.clay.com/guides/clay-mcp exposing data providers, AI research agents, and workflows inside AI assistants. Community/open-source MCP server also exists at https://github.com/clay-inc/clay-mcp.
buildability_blocker: Potential higher-tier paid plan required for HTTP/API access and unclear scope of direct public API.
buildability_detail: Clay appears buildable today because it has self-serve signup, documented HTTP API integration capabilities, and standard authentication methods. Caveats are that API access may require expensive paid plans and search results do not clearly show a comprehensive public platform API for all objects/features.

one_line_description: Code hosting and collaboration platform with APIs for repositories, issues, pull requests, actions, and more.
auth_details: GitHub REST API supports token-based authentication including personal access tokens, OAuth tokens, and GitHub App installation tokens. Docs state authenticated requests require an authentication token with appropriate scopes or permissions.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create GitHub accounts and obtain API access credentials such as personal access tokens through self-service signup. GitHub offers a free plan.
api_breadth_detail: GitHub provides a comprehensive REST API covering repositories, users, issues, pull requests, billing, GitHub Apps, Actions, and many other platform features. The API is documented with an OpenAPI description.
mcp_server_detail: GitHub documents MCP support for GitHub Copilot and references a GitHub MCP server and MCP Registry. Docs mention 'Using the GitHub MCP Server in your IDE' and the github/github-mcp-server repository.
buildability_detail: GitHub has a mature public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding, and standard token/OAuth authentication, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit.

one_line_description: Cloud platform for deploying, scaling, and managing web applications and developer infrastructure.
auth_details: The Vercel REST API requires Vercel Access Tokens to authenticate API requests. AI Gateway supports API keys and OIDC tokens. Search results also reference Sign in with Vercel using OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect for developer authentication.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create and manage access tokens in their Vercel account settings and Vercel offers a free Hobby plan for developers. Public docs and signup flows are available without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: Comprehensive REST API covering deployments, projects, domains, DNS, teams, logs, webhooks, edge config, billing, security, feature flags, sandboxes, integrations, analytics, and many other resources with dozens of endpoint groups.
mcp_server_detail: Vercel provides MCP documentation and tooling including an MCP adapter for Next.js apps. Docs explain MCP architecture and available MCP servers; community examples show building remote MCP servers with Vercel's MCP Adapter. Sources: https://vercel.com/docs/mcp and https://medium.com/@kevin.moechel/building-a-remote-mcp-server-with-next-js-and-vercels-mcp-adapter-d078b27a9119
buildability_detail: Vercel has a public self-serve REST API with standard token/API key authentication, extensive endpoint coverage, public documentation, and accessible developer onboarding. Composio could build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Web hosting and deployment platform for the programmable web with APIs for sites, deploys, forms, DNS, and more.
auth_details: Netlify's public API uses OAuth 2 for authentication. The MCP server documentation also references using a Netlify Personal Access Token (PAT) for authentication.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for Netlify's always-free self-serve plan and access platform features without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: REST-style JSON API with extensive coverage across accounts, sites, deploys, environment variables, snippets, DNS, databases, billing, forms, and more via many endpoints documented in the OpenAPI reference.
mcp_server_detail: Official Netlify MCP server available at https://github.com/netlify/netlify-mcp. It enables AI agents to use the Netlify API and CLI to create projects, deploy, and manage Netlify resources. Netlify also announced the official MCP server publicly in 2025.
buildability_detail: Netlify provides a public REST API with OAuth2 authentication, broad endpoint coverage, self-serve developer onboarding via a free plan, and an official MCP server, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Cloud platform providing CDN, DNS, security, serverless, storage, and developer infrastructure APIs.
auth_details: Cloudflare APIs support API Tokens for authenticated API access and legacy Global API Keys. Cloudflare MCP remote connections also mention OAuth authorization for MCP clients.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create Cloudflare accounts and access free plans such as Workers Free and R2 free usage tiers without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: Cloudflare exposes extensive REST APIs across accounts, zones, DNS, load balancers, Workers, R2, Zero Trust, AI, and more, with over 2,500 endpoints referenced for the MCP server. Cloudflare Analytics also provides a GraphQL API.
mcp_server_detail: Cloudflare provides official MCP support and managed MCP servers. The Cloudflare API MCP server exposes access to the full Cloudflare API (over 2,500 endpoints) through MCP tools. Docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/cloudflare/servers-for-cloudflare
buildability_detail: Cloudflare offers public REST and GraphQL APIs, self-serve developer onboarding with free plans, standard token/API-key auth, and official MCP server support, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Open-source backend platform providing Postgres database, authentication, storage, edge functions, and APIs for developers.
auth_details: Supabase Auth uses JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) for authentication. SDK requests are sent with the user's auth token. Supabase supports multiple auth flows including password, OTP, social login, and SSO.
self_serve_detail: Supabase offers a publicly accessible free tier with limits on database size, storage, bandwidth, and active projects; developers can sign up and start using the platform without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: Supabase exposes broad platform functionality including authentication, database access, storage, and edge functions through APIs and SDKs. Search results specifically reference Auth APIs and integration with database features.
mcp_server_detail: Supabase provides an official MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for connecting AI tools to Supabase projects, enabling database management and natural language operations. Official feature page: https://supabase.com/features/mcp-server . Community implementation also exists at https://github.com/coleam00/supabase-mcp
buildability_detail: Supabase has public developer documentation, self-serve signup with a free tier, standard token/JWT-based authentication, and broad API coverage. An official MCP server further supports AI agent integrations.

one_line_description: Graph database platform and managed graph database service with HTTP APIs and AI/MCP integrations.
auth_details: Neo4j HTTP API supports Authorization headers using Basic authentication (base64 username:password) and Bearer token authentication.
self_serve_detail: Neo4j offers AuraDB Free tier allowing developers to learn, test, prototype, and build applications without barriers.
api_breadth_detail: Neo4j exposes an HTTP API for database operations and transactions, along with authentication/authorization support and extensibility plugins. Coverage appears broad for graph database interactions and administration.
mcp_server_detail: Official Neo4j MCP server/documentation exists. Neo4j MCP provides structured access to Neo4j graph databases for MCP-compatible AI clients. Community GitHub repo also exists at https://github.com/neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j.
buildability_detail: Neo4j provides public HTTP APIs, standard authentication methods, self-serve free-tier developer access, and official MCP support, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Cloud data platform for data warehousing, analytics, AI, and developer data applications.
auth_details: Snowflake REST APIs support programmatic access tokens (PATs), key pair authentication with generated JWT tokens, OAuth-based authentication for managed MCP integrations, username/password authentication, SSO via browser/Okta, and private-key authentication methods.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for Snowflake accounts and use usage-based/free-trial access. Search results reference free trial credits and publicly accessible developer guides and marketplace listings.
api_breadth_detail: Snowflake exposes multiple REST APIs and developer interfaces covering SQL API, Cortex APIs, authentication, drivers, AI services, and broader data platform operations. Documentation suggests extensive platform coverage across core Snowflake capabilities.
mcp_server_detail: Snowflake provides an official Snowflake-managed MCP server in public preview supporting Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, Cortex Agents, custom tools, and SQL execution. Community MCP servers also exist for Snowflake database access.
buildability_detail: Snowflake has public developer documentation, standard authentication mechanisms, broad REST API coverage, and self-serve developer access, making it feasible to build a Composio toolkit today.

one_line_description: Managed multi-cloud MongoDB database platform with administration APIs for clusters, users, and infrastructure.
auth_details: Atlas Administration API supports Service Accounts using OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow to obtain Bearer access tokens, as well as API Keys. Atlas authentication guidance also mentions SAML 2.0 federated authentication, X.509 certificates, and SCRAM for some Atlas resources.
self_serve_detail: MongoDB Atlas offers a free tier/free cluster for learning, development, and testing. Developers can sign up directly and access Atlas services and APIs without requiring sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: MongoDB Atlas Administration API v2 exposes endpoints to manage organizations, projects, clusters, users, networking, and other Atlas components. Documentation describes it as allowing developers to manage all components in MongoDB Atlas.
mcp_server_detail: Official MongoDB MCP Server exists. GitHub repository mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server and official Docker image support interacting with MongoDB databases and MongoDB Atlas using Atlas API credentials or MongoDB connection strings. Community listing also exists on MCP Market. URLs: https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server , https://hub.docker.com/r/mongodb/mongodb-mcp-server , https://mcpmarket.com/server/mongodb-atlas
buildability_detail: MongoDB Atlas provides a public REST administration API with standard OAuth2/API key authentication and self-serve developer onboarding via a free tier. Existing official MCP server further validates integration feasibility.

one_line_description: Cloud observability and monitoring platform for infrastructure, applications, logs, and security.
auth_details: Datadog API authenticates using API keys via the `DD-API-KEY` header; documentation also references Application Keys used alongside API keys.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access Datadog through public signup/pricing flows; API documentation is publicly available and API/application keys are referenced as user-manageable credentials.
api_breadth_detail: Public HTTP REST API covering major Datadog platform capabilities including metrics, logs, dashboards, monitors, integrations, and agent/integration management across many endpoint groups.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP server exists: 'Datadog MCP Server' by magistersart with GitHub/Docker distribution, using Datadog API and application keys. Evidence: https://lobehub.com/mcp/magistersart-dd-mcp . Datadog also publishes educational content about MCP servers: https://www.datadoghq.com/knowledge-center/mcp-server
buildability_detail: Datadog exposes a public REST API with standard API key authentication and publicly accessible developer documentation, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Application monitoring and error tracking platform for developers.
auth_details: Sentry API supports Bearer authentication tokens in the Authorization header for user or organization access. Sentry also supports OAuth2 authorization code grant for third-party applications accessing Sentry on behalf of users.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for Sentry directly and use a free Developer plan with usage limits. API docs and auth token creation tutorials are publicly available.
api_breadth_detail: Public REST API (v0) covers organizations, projects, teams, authentication, and broader Sentry platform functionality through many documented endpoints and tutorials.
mcp_server_detail: Sentry provides official MCP monitoring documentation for Model Context Protocol implementations. Community MCP servers also exist for accessing and analyzing Sentry issues and debugging information. Evidence: https://docs.sentry.io/ai/monitoring/mcp and https://mcpmarket.com/server/sentry
buildability_detail: Sentry has a public REST API, standard token/OAuth2 authentication, public documentation, and self-serve developer signup with a free tier, making it suitable for building an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Workspace and productivity platform for docs, databases, projects, and collaboration.
auth_details: Notion supports OAuth 2.0 for public connections and static bearer tokens for internal connections and personal access tokens (PATs). API requests authenticate using the HTTP Authorization header with Bearer tokens.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create connections and retrieve installation access tokens through the Notion Developer portal without requiring a partnership or sales approval. Search results also indicate API access is available on free plans.
api_breadth_detail: The REST API covers pages, databases/data sources, users, blocks, comments, search, pagination, and workspace interactions. Documentation references a wide range of objects and endpoints across core Notion functionality.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist for Notion, including the npm package 'notion-mcp-server' and the GitHub project 'suekou/mcp-notion-server', which expose Notion API operations to MCP-compatible AI clients. URLs: https://npmjs.com/package/notion-mcp-server?ref=pkgstats.com and https://github.com/suekou/mcp-notion-server
buildability_detail: Notion provides a public REST API with standard OAuth2 and bearer token authentication, self-serve developer onboarding, and broad API coverage. Existing MCP server implementations further demonstrate ecosystem readiness for agent tooling.

one_line_description: Low-code collaborative database and app platform with a public developer API.
auth_details: Airtable Web API uses bearer token authentication. Supported token types include Personal Access Tokens for personal/server integrations and OAuth access tokens for multi-user integrations. Legacy User API Keys are deprecated but documented in third-party references.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up and create personal access tokens or OAuth apps through Airtable's developer portal. Airtable advertises a free plan ('Get started for free').
api_breadth_detail: The Web API includes authentication, scopes, OAuth, CRUD operations, list bases, user info, org management, billing plans, rate limits, and other endpoints covering core Airtable platform functionality.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Airtable, including 'airtable-mcp-server' and listings on mcpservers.org and MCP Market. They support schema discovery and CRUD operations using Airtable Personal Access Tokens. Sources: https://mcpservers.org/servers/felores/airtable-mcp and https://www.augmentcode.com/mcp/airtable-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Airtable has a public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding, OAuth2 and token-based authentication, and broad API coverage. Community MCP implementations also exist, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Developer-focused issue tracking and project management platform with a GraphQL API and SDK.
auth_details: Linear supports OAuth 2.0 authentication for integrations and personal API keys for direct API access. OAuth apps use client ID, client secret, redirect URLs, and scopes such as read and app.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-sign up via Linear's free plan and create OAuth2 applications or personal API keys without requiring sales approval. Pricing page includes a free tier with signup access.
api_breadth_detail: Linear provides a GraphQL API covering issues, projects, teams, workflows, uploads, agents, and other workspace data, along with a TypeScript SDK. Apollo Studio describes access to all Linear data.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Linear, including Remote MCP and open-source Linear MCP Server implementations that expose Linear GraphQL API operations for AI assistants. Examples: https://www.remote-mcp.com/servers/linear and https://mcpservers.org/servers/linear-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Linear has a public GraphQL API, supports standard OAuth2 and API key authentication, offers self-serve signup with a free tier, and has existing MCP ecosystem support, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit.

one_line_description: Project management and issue tracking platform by Atlassian.
auth_details: Jira Cloud REST APIs support Basic authentication using Atlassian account email + API token. Atlassian docs also mention Forge apps using OAuth 2.0 and Connect apps using JWT. MCP examples reference Personal Access Tokens for Server/Data Center deployments.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-sign up for Jira Cloud. Atlassian offers a free plan for up to 10 users and free trials for Standard/Premium plans, enabling self-serve API access.
api_breadth_detail: Extensive REST API covering boards, issues, sprints, projects, dashboards, users, permissions, workflows, search/JQL, attachments, comments, notifications, and many administrative resources across dozens of endpoint groups.
mcp_server_detail: Community/open-source MCP servers exist for Jira/Atlassian products, including the 'mcp-atlassian' project on PyPI supporting Jira Cloud and Server/Data Center. Additional guides from Workato and Medium describe Jira MCP server implementations.
buildability_detail: Jira provides a public REST API with broad coverage, self-serve developer access via free plans/trials, and standard authentication methods including OAuth2 and API tokens/basic auth. Existing MCP ecosystem support further lowers integration friction.

one_line_description: Project management and work tracking platform with tasks, projects, workflows, and collaboration APIs.
auth_details: Asana supports OAuth for applications acting on behalf of users and personal access tokens (PATs) for simpler API access. PATs and OAuth tokens are passed in the Authorization header.
self_serve_detail: Developers can self-serve by creating a free Asana account and generating personal access tokens from the Asana developer console. Asana also offers a free Personal plan.
api_breadth_detail: Asana provides a REST API covering tasks, projects, workspaces, memberships, workflows, portfolios, and other core Asana Work Graph resources. Documentation references multiple endpoint groups and broad platform access.
mcp_server_detail: Asana provides an official MCP server that allows AI assistants and tools to access and interact with the Asana Work Graph. Docs and compatible clients are published by Asana. References: https://developers.asana.com/docs/mcp-server and https://developers.asana.com/docs/mcp-clients
buildability_detail: Asana has a public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding with PATs and OAuth, and official MCP support, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Work operating system for project management, workflows, automations, and collaboration.
auth_details: The monday.com platform API supports personal V2 API tokens passed in the Authorization header. Apps can also authenticate using OAuth access tokens via https://auth.monday.com/oauth2/token. monday SDK seamless authentication is also referenced for in-app calls.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create a free, no-expiration developer account and access developer tools including the API and apps framework without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: The platform API uses GraphQL and provides broad coverage across boards, leads, docs, updates, workflows, automations, integrations, and more.
mcp_server_detail: Official monday.com MCP server exists. monday.com provides hosted MCP support and an official GitHub repository with MCP server packages such as @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp. Docs describe the MCP server as a wrapper around the monday.com Platform API. Sources: https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/docs/monday-mcp-security-overview and https://github.com/mondaycom/mcp
buildability_detail: Monday.com has a public GraphQL API with self-serve developer access, standard token and OAuth2 authentication, broad API coverage, and official MCP tooling. Composio could build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Project management and productivity platform with tasks, docs, views, automations, and collaboration features.
auth_details: ClickUp API supports personal API tokens for individual/testing use and OAuth for apps/integrations used by others. Requests include the token in the Authorization header. OAuth token exchange uses client_id, client_secret, and authorization code via /oauth/token.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for a ClickUp account, generate a personal API token themselves, and use the public API docs including Try-It features. ClickUp offers a freemium plan.
api_breadth_detail: Public REST API covers tasks, custom fields, views, communication, webhooks, workspaces, and more across API v2/v3 documentation. Docs indicate broad integration support and many endpoint categories.
mcp_server_detail: Official ClickUp MCP server is available at https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp and supports AI assistants interacting with tasks, lists, folders, and docs. Official docs: https://developer.clickup.com/docs/connect-an-ai-assistant-to-clickups-mcp-server . Community MCP implementations also exist such as https://github.com/Nazruden/clickup-mcp-server
buildability_detail: ClickUp provides a public REST API with self-serve developer access, standard OAuth2 and personal token authentication, interactive docs, and official MCP support. Composio could build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Collaborative docs and project management platform with programmable tables, pages, and automations.
auth_details: Coda API uses bearer access tokens passed in the Authorization header (e.g. 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'). Developers can generate API access tokens in Coda account settings.
self_serve_detail: Coda API is available to all users including free workspaces. Developers can self-sign up and generate API access tokens without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: REST API covers docs, tables, rows, pages, permissions, analytics, and other core Coda resources with many endpoints across workspace/document functionality.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist for Coda, including orellazri/coda-mcp on GitHub. These provide tools for listing, reading, creating, updating, duplicating, and renaming Coda pages and tables via the Coda API. Not officially maintained by Coda. Sources: https://github.com/orellazri/coda-mcp and https://lobehub.com/mcp/tjc-lp-coda-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Coda exposes a public REST API with straightforward bearer token authentication and self-serve developer access available on free workspaces, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Work management and collaboration platform with sheets, project tracking, automation, and APIs.
auth_details: Smartsheet supports OAuth2 for third-party applications and access tokens/API tokens for direct API access. Documentation references OAuth2 flow and manually generated access tokens used to access Smartsheet data.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access public developer docs, register developer tools/applications, and generate API access tokens themselves. API access is restricted to Business and Enterprise plans according to API reference docs.
api_breadth_detail: Comprehensive REST API with OpenAPI reference covering users, sheets, rows, columns, comments, attachments, workspaces, and other core Smartsheet resources. Includes SDKs and samples for multiple languages.
mcp_server_detail: Official Smartsheet MCP Server announced by Smartsheet, providing read/write access to Sheets, Rows, Columns, Discussions, Comments, and Workspaces via Model Context Protocol. Community MCP servers also exist on GitHub and mcpservers.org. Official announcement: https://www.smartsheet.com/content-center/product-insights/product-updates/introducing-smartsheet-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Smartsheet offers a public REST API, OAuth2 and token-based authentication, SDKs, OpenAPI documentation, and self-serve developer onboarding. Some API functionality may require Business or Enterprise plans, but the platform is generally accessible for integration development.

one_line_description: Time tracking and project management platform with a public API for managing accounts, projects, users, and time entries.
auth_details: Harvest API v2 supports Personal Access Tokens used as Bearer tokens in the Authorization header (or query string) along with a required Harvest account ID. Search results also indicate support for OAuth 2.0.
self_serve_detail: All Harvest accounts, including free and trial accounts, include API access. Developers can create Personal Access Tokens from the Developers section of Harvest ID without partnership approval.
api_breadth_detail: REST API v2 covers major Harvest functionality including time entries, projects, clients, users, assignments, billing rates, and account management. MCP listings reference 64 API endpoints exposed.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple unofficial community MCP servers exist for Harvest API v2, including a Go-based server exposing all 64 Harvest API endpoints and a TypeScript MCP server for time tracking/project management. Sources: https://lobehub.com/mcp/valtirallc-harvest-mcp-server and https://mcpservers.org/servers/ianaleck/harvest-mcp-server
buildability_detail: Harvest provides a public REST API with self-serve access for free and trial accounts plus standard token/OAuth authentication, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Online payments and financial infrastructure platform with APIs for payments, billing, subscriptions, payouts, and more.
auth_details: Stripe API authenticates primarily with secret and restricted API keys managed in the Stripe Dashboard. Stripe Apps also support OAuth 2.0 access tokens for acting on behalf of user accounts.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for Stripe, access API documentation, create test and live API keys from the Stripe Dashboard, and test integrations in sandbox mode without sales approval.
api_breadth_detail: Stripe exposes a very large REST API surface covering payments, customers, billing, subscriptions, invoicing, payouts, accounts, products, checkout, tax, treasury-related resources, and many more endpoints across hundreds of resources.
mcp_server_detail: Stripe provides an official MCP server documented by Stripe. It allows AI agents to interact with the Stripe API and knowledge base, with tools for API reads/writes and search. Docs: https://docs.stripe.com/mcp
buildability_detail: Stripe has a public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding, standard API key/OAuth authentication, extensive documentation, SDKs, and an official MCP server, making it straightforward to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Financial data network and API platform for connecting bank accounts, transactions, identity, and payment-related data.
auth_details: Plaid provides OAuth endpoints such as /oauth/token for creating and refreshing OAuth access tokens. Plaid integrations also use client_id and secret credentials for API access, commonly treated as API-key style credentials, and access tokens are exchanged/used for Item access.
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up for a Plaid developer account and use the Sandbox environment for free. Plaid also offers free Trial/Limited Production access for testing with production data, though full production access may require additional application review, company information, agreements, and security questionnaires.
api_breadth_detail: Plaid exposes a broad REST API surface covering auth/account verification, transactions, balances, identity, AML/sanctions, statements, risk, and other banking/fintech capabilities across many endpoints and products.
mcp_server_detail: Plaid docs reference a Plaid MCP Server, and community MCP servers also exist for Plaid sandbox integrations. Plaid additionally published an engineering blog about its internal MCP server. Community example: https://lobehub.com/nl/mcp/argotdev-plaid-mcp-ts
buildability_blocker: Production access review and compliance requirements
buildability_detail: Plaid has a public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding, and standard authentication mechanisms. However, moving beyond sandbox/trial usage into full production access can require approval steps, contracts, and compliance/security review.

one_line_description: Cryptocurrency exchange platform offering trading, market data, payments, and financial APIs.
auth_details: Binance APIs use API keys for authentication, typically passed in the X-MBX-APIKEY header. Signed endpoints require request signatures using a secret key (HMAC). Binance Pay merchant APIs also use API keys managed in the Merchant Admin Portal.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access API documentation publicly and use Binance Spot Testnet or Binance Demo for free testing. API keys can be created through Binance account portals without requiring partnership approval.
api_breadth_detail: Extensive API coverage across spot trading, margin, futures, options, wallet, payments, market data, and WebSocket streaming. Documentation includes many trading/order/account endpoints and SDK examples.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple unofficial community MCP servers exist for Binance, including https://github.com/AnalyticAce/binance-mcp-server and https://github.com/TermiX-official/binance-mcp. These support trading, market data, account management, and AI agent integrations via MCP.
buildability_detail: Binance provides extensive public APIs, self-serve developer onboarding, standard API key/HMAC authentication, testnet environments, and broad trading/account functionality, making it feasible to build a Composio toolkit today.

one_line_description: Payment processing and fintech API platform powered by NMI/Paya Connect.
auth_details: Authentication docs describe using user_id and user_api_key in headers or query parameters, or via HTTP Basic Authentication. Docs also reference POST /v2/token using username, password, and domain to obtain a token. A developer-id header or query parameter is required.
self_serve_detail: Developer access appears gated behind an application/request workflow. Docs state: 'Click here to fill out the Developer Portal application to request access.' No evidence of instant self-service signup or free tier was found.
api_breadth_detail: Developer docs reference a REST API with authentication, API reference, quick start guide, request logs, and Postman environment support. Exact endpoint count is not provided in the search results, but coverage appears to include core payment platform functionality.
mcp_server_detail: No official or community MCP server for Paygent Connect/Paya Connect was found in the provided search results.
buildability_blocker: Developer portal access requires application/request approval.
buildability_detail: A public REST API with standard authentication methods exists, so integration is technically feasible. However, developer credentials appear gated behind a portal access request rather than instant self-service signup, which may slow onboarding.

one_line_description: Unknown fintech/payment-related platform with limited publicly discoverable API information from provided search results.
auth_details: No direct iPayX authentication documentation was found in the provided search results. Results referenced unrelated payment APIs using API keys, certificates/JWT assertions, and Basic auth, but none could be confidently attributed to iPayX.
self_serve_detail: Unknown. No evidence in the provided results of a public developer signup flow, free tier, or self-serve credential issuance for iPayX.
api_breadth_detail: The provided search results did not expose concrete API reference details, endpoint coverage, or protocol information for iPayX.
mcp_server_detail: No iPayX-specific MCP server was found in the provided search results. Results only described MCP conceptually.
buildability_blocker: Insufficient public API and authentication information
buildability_detail: Based strictly on the provided search results, there is not enough evidence of a publicly documented API, self-serve developer onboarding, or supported authentication model to determine that Composio could build an integration today.

one_line_description: Cloud accounting and financial management platform with APIs for QuickBooks Online and related Intuit services.
auth_details: QuickBooks Online APIs use OAuth 2.0 for authentication and authorization. Developers create an app in the Intuit Developer Portal, obtain a Client ID and Client Secret, and implement a user consent flow to access customer data.
self_serve_detail: Developers can register on the Intuit Developer Portal, create apps, obtain credentials, and use sandbox environments without requiring partnership approval. Search results also indicate free developer registration and integration access.
api_breadth_detail: QuickBooks Online exposes extensive accounting and finance APIs including accounting entities, reports, taxes, projects, payments, and related workflows. Documentation references REST APIs plus GraphQL support, multiple SDKs, and broad CRUD/reporting coverage across many resources.
mcp_server_detail: Official open-source MCP server exists at Intuit GitHub repository: https://github.com/intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server . It provides comprehensive QuickBooks Online API integration with CRUD operations for 29 entity types and 11 financial reports using MCP-compatible clients.
buildability_detail: QuickBooks provides public developer documentation, self-serve developer onboarding, OAuth2 authentication, sandbox testing, and broad API coverage. An official MCP server also exists, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Cloud accounting and business finance platform with APIs for accounting, payroll, invoices, contacts, and related business data.
auth_details: Xero public APIs use OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow and PKCE flow. Apps receive a Client ID and can generate client secrets. MCP server docs also mention bearer token authentication support for custom connections.
self_serve_detail: Developers can create OAuth2 apps through the Xero Developer platform and access Starter/free tier developer access. Pricing page describes multiple developer tiers including Starter. Search results also mention new apps defaulting to the free Starter tier with limits.
api_breadth_detail: Xero provides broad accounting and business APIs with official SDKs and OpenAPI specs covering accounting, invoices, contacts, reports, bank transactions, payroll, and more. Public repositories include SDKs for Node, Python, Java, PHP, Ruby, and OpenAPI definitions.
mcp_server_detail: Official open-source MCP server exists at XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server. It bridges MCP with Xero APIs and supports accounting operations such as contacts, invoices, reports, bank transactions, and payroll. Available via GitHub and npm.
buildability_detail: Xero has a public REST API, self-serve developer onboarding, standard OAuth2 authentication, official SDKs/OpenAPI specs, and an official MCP server. Composio could build an agent toolkit today. Caveat: Xero pricing and updated developer terms include restrictions around AI/ML training use of API data.

one_line_description: Financial platform API for managing expenses, spend limits, payments, cards, and related business finance workflows.
auth_details: Brex client APIs use user tokens generated from the Brex dashboard and passed in API headers. Partner integrations support OAuth2 authorization flows with authorization code exchange and scoped access tokens.
self_serve_detail: Developers can access the developer portal at developer.brex.com, create/register applications, obtain API credentials, and test in a sandbox environment without evidence of mandatory sales approval in the provided results.
api_breadth_detail: Brex exposes APIs for spend limits, expenses, fields, payments, vendors, virtual cards, and related finance workflows, indicating broad operational coverage across the platform.
mcp_server_detail: A community MCP server exists at https://github.com/crazyrabbitLTC/mcp-brex-server providing read-only Brex expense and transaction access for AI agents. MCP listings also appear on MCP Market: https://mcpmarket.com/server/brex
buildability_detail: Brex provides public REST APIs with documented authentication, developer onboarding, sandbox testing, and standard token/OAuth2 auth flows, making it feasible to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: Corporate finance platform offering spend management, cards, expenses, and financial operations APIs.
auth_details: Ramp authenticates token requests to /developer/v1/token using HTTP Basic Auth with base64-encoded client_id:client_secret. Subsequent API calls use Bearer access tokens in the Authorization header. Support article also refers to OAuth2 credentials (Client ID and Client Secret) for sandbox and production apps.
self_serve_detail: Developers who are Ramp customers with admin access can create a developer app directly in the Ramp dashboard to obtain credentials. Sandbox environment is available for testing. Production access may require applying after testing.
api_breadth_detail: Public REST API with endpoints for transactions and broader financial workflows/integrations referenced in developer docs and partner integrations. Search results indicate multiple resources and sandbox/production environments, but full endpoint breadth was not provided.
mcp_server_detail: Community/third-party MCP servers exist for Ramp, including 'ramp-mcp' and Ramp Developer MCP listings. Ramp also published a blog post titled 'Building Ramp's MCP server'. Evidence: https://builders.ramp.com/post/ramp-mcp and https://mcpmarket.com/server/ramp-developer
buildability_blocker: Requires Ramp customer account with admin access; production access may require application approval.
buildability_detail: Ramp exposes a public REST API with standard authentication and sandbox support, making toolkit development feasible. However, obtaining credentials requires being a Ramp customer with admin access, and production access may involve an approval/application step.

one_line_description: Private market data and investment analytics platform with API access to companies, deals, investors, funds, and market intelligence.
auth_details: Public API V2 docs specify including an 'authorization' header with value format 'PB-Token {API_KEY}' on each request.
self_serve_detail: PitchBook markets API access and offers a 'Request a free trial' flow rather than an open self-serve developer signup. Search results do not show instant self-service credential issuance.
api_breadth_detail: RESTful API v2 provides real-time access to extensive datasets including companies, deals, people, investors, funds, and service providers, indicating broad coverage across the platform.
mcp_server_detail: PitchBook announced a Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector integration with OpenAI/ChatGPT for subscribers, and third-party reporting describes PitchBook MCP apps available in ChatGPT.
buildability_blocker: API access appears gated behind commercial subscription/trial approval rather than fully self-serve.
buildability_detail: PitchBook has a documented public REST API with standard token/API-key authentication and broad data coverage. However, developer access appears commercially gated via trial request/subscription rather than instant self-service onboarding, which may slow toolkit deployment.

one_line_description: Google's AI-powered research and note synthesis tool for grounded answers and content generation from uploaded sources.
auth_details: NotebookLM Enterprise API is hosted on Google Cloud endpoints and uses Google Cloud IAM/project-based access. Exact auth flow is not explicitly shown in the provided docs, but Google Cloud APIs typically use OAuth2/service account auth. Community MCP servers authenticate by logging into a Google account in a browser session with persisted cookies.
self_serve_detail: NotebookLM has a free consumer tier and developers can access NotebookLM Enterprise through Google Cloud. However, the official API appears tied to Enterprise/Google Cloud access and may require a Google Cloud project. Search results indicate Enterprise-only API availability.
api_breadth_detail: Official NotebookLM Enterprise API exposes notebook CRUD and sharing operations via REST endpoints under discoveryengine.googleapis.com. Community reverse-engineered APIs expose roughly 33 endpoints including source ingestion and content generation.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist, including PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp and notebooklm-mcp-cli. They provide programmatic access to NotebookLM via browser automation and expose tools for notebook management, grounded chat, source ingestion, and audio generation. MCP directory listing: https://mcp.directory/servers/notebooklm ; GitHub: https://github.com/PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp
buildability_blocker: Enterprise-oriented access and unclear official public API availability for non-enterprise users.
buildability_detail: Composio could likely build an integration using the NotebookLM Enterprise REST API or community MCP/browser automation tooling. However, official API access appears enterprise-scoped and public availability has historically been limited, creating onboarding and stability caveats.

one_line_description: AI meeting assistant and transcription platform with APIs for conversations, transcripts, audio, insights, and workspace data.
auth_details: Otter public API documentation includes an Authentication section. Additional API reference states the Authorization API is based on OAuth 2.0 supporting Client Credentials and Authorization Code flows, using Bearer tokens in the Authorization header.
self_serve_detail: Otter.ai offers self-serve signup with a free tier ('Start for free'). Public API documentation is publicly accessible. Search results also mention a free Basic tier with limited transcription minutes.
api_breadth_detail: Public REST API exposes channels, channel members, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, workspace details, and webhooks. Documentation lists multiple GET and POST endpoints under /channels, /conversations, and /workspace.
mcp_server_detail: Official Otter MCP Server documented by Otter Help Center with setup guides for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Perplexity, and other AI tools. Includes tools overview and permissions configuration.
buildability_detail: Otter AI has a public REST API, documented OAuth2/Bearer token authentication, self-serve signup/free tier, and an official MCP server. Composio could build an agent toolkit today using the available API and MCP integrations.

one_line_description: AI meeting assistant platform with recordings, transcripts, summaries, action items, and integrations.
auth_details: Fathom REST API supports API key authentication via keys generated in the Fathom settings area, bearer token authentication in SDKs, and mentions OAuth for multi-user integrations and partner OAuth apps.
self_serve_detail: Public API is available and anyone can browse the API docs and start building. API keys are created at the user level through the Fathom settings area. Fathom also offers a free product tier according to public pricing pages.
api_breadth_detail: REST API covers meeting summaries, transcripts, recordings, webhooks, teams, analytics, search, and related meeting data operations. Official Python and TypeScript SDKs are available.
mcp_server_detail: Fathom provides an official MCP server at https://api.fathom.ai/mcp documented in their developer docs. Community MCP servers also exist, including https://github.com/Dot-Fun/fathom-mcp and https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lengelhard/fathom-mcp.
buildability_detail: Fathom has a public REST API with self-serve API keys, official SDKs, public documentation, and an official MCP server, making it feasible for Composio to build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: AI-powered academic research search and synthesis platform with API access to peer-reviewed paper search results.
auth_details: Consensus API docs mention entering 'API and User Credentials' and generating API credentials from the Integrations section of the web app. The official remote MCP server uses OAuth sign-in/authorization when connecting from MCP clients.
self_serve_detail: Developers with a Consensus account can generate API credentials themselves from the Integrations section in the web app. Public API marketing page is available, but free tier/trial details are not clearly stated in the provided results.
api_breadth_detail: Consensus exposes an Open API for embedding Consensus search results and automating research workflows. The API supports search queries, filtering papers by study design/country, and returning ranked paper results. Breadth appears focused on research search/intelligence features rather than the entire product surface.
mcp_server_detail: Official remote MCP server documented at https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp. Supports connecting AI assistants to Consensus research search capabilities. MCP setup guide states OAuth authentication is required on first connection.
buildability_blocker: API access details and pricing/free-tier availability are not fully transparent in provided results.
buildability_detail: Consensus has a public Open API with self-serve credential generation and an official MCP server. However, authentication specifics and developer onboarding/pricing details are somewhat sparse in the provided search results, creating some uncertainty around friction and limits.

one_line_description: Agentic document platform for parsing, extracting, splitting, classifying, and editing documents into structured JSON for AI workflows.
auth_details: API requests are authenticated using API keys managed in Reducto Studio. Docs state 'API keys authenticate your requests to Reducto.'
self_serve_detail: Developers can sign up via Reducto Studio and start on a free tier with up to 15K credits. Pricing page includes 'Get started' and 'Try for free' links without indicating sales approval is required for basic access.
api_breadth_detail: Public API supports document parsing and broader document operations including parse, extract, split, classify, edit, uploads, usage export, and webhooks. Documentation and SDK quickstart indicate substantial coverage of core platform capabilities.
mcp_server_detail: Official Reducto MCP server documented by Reducto. Supports Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, and other MCP clients for classify, parse, extract, split, and edit operations. Docs: https://docs.reducto.ai/mcp-server
buildability_detail: Reducto provides a public API with self-serve signup/free credits, API key authentication, developer documentation, SDK examples, and an official MCP server. Composio could build an agent toolkit today.

one_line_description: AI software engineering agent platform for creating and managing autonomous coding sessions and workflows.
auth_details: The Devin API uses a 'principal + token' authentication model according to official docs. MindCloud's Devin integration authenticates with a Bearer token in the Authorization header using a MindCloud API key. Devin CLI enterprise auth also supports SSO/identity-provider login for enterprise organizations.
self_serve_detail: Devin offers self-serve plans including a Free plan with light quota access to coding agents and cloud agents. Enterprise-only features exist for some CLI authentication flows, but core product access appears self-serve.
api_breadth_detail: Public API documentation references management of Devin sessions, knowledge, playbooks, secrets, schedules, and organization resources. Search results suggest a reasonably broad REST API for core platform operations, though complete endpoint coverage is unclear.
mcp_server_detail: Devin is officially MCP-compatible via Devin's MCP Marketplace, allowing integration with MCP servers. Additionally, an official DeepWiki by Devin MCP server is listed at https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp.
buildability_blocker: Authentication and API details are partially unclear from public search results.
buildability_detail: Devin appears to have a public REST API, self-serve signup/pricing, and token-based authentication, making toolkit development feasible. However, the exact public API onboarding flow and auth implementation details are not fully exposed in the provided results, and some capabilities are enterprise-gated.

one_line_description: AI media generation platform for creating images, videos, voices, and cinematic content.
auth_details: Search results indicate API key authentication for API access and hosted MCP access via browser OAuth. MindCloud docs specify Bearer token authentication using a MindCloud API key in the Authorization header. Community MCP server examples require HF_API_KEY and HF_SECRET environment variables.
self_serve_detail: Public pricing page and free plan references suggest developers can self-serve sign up and access the platform. However, third-party commentary suggests API access may be gated to higher-tier paid plans and documentation is sparse.
api_breadth_detail: Search results reference endpoints/modules for character management, motion generation, image generation, speech-to-video, listing styles and motions, and generic API calls. Coverage appears to include core AI media generation workflows but breadth of official public API is unclear.
mcp_server_detail: Both community and hosted MCP servers exist. Community server: https://github.com/geopopos/higgsfield_ai_mcp using HF_API_KEY and HF_SECRET. Hosted MCP endpoint reported at https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp with OAuth authentication for Claude Code and compatible clients.
buildability_blocker: Official API access/documentation appears limited or gated behind paid tiers; unclear official developer support.
buildability_detail: There is evidence of REST-style API access, API key authentication, self-serve signup, and multiple MCP server implementations. However, much of the evidence comes from third parties/community tooling rather than official developer docs, and search results suggest API access may require higher-tier plans with sparse documentation.

one_line_description: Command-line tool for rendering and validating Mermaid diagrams.
auth_details: Mermaid CLI is a local/open-source CLI tool and the provided search results do not indicate any API authentication mechanism.
self_serve_detail: Open-source project hosted on GitHub; developers can install directly via npm without sales approval or account gating.
api_breadth_detail: Primarily a command-line interface for validating and rendering Mermaid diagrams rather than a hosted API. Coverage appears limited to diagram rendering/validation workflows.
mcp_server_detail: Community MCP servers exist that wrap Mermaid CLI functionality, including https://github.com/andrewginns/mermaid-mcp-server and Mermaid Validator MCP listings on LobeHub and mcp.so. These servers validate and render Mermaid diagrams using Mermaid CLI.
buildability_detail: Although Mermaid CLI is not a traditional web API, it is open source, self-serve, and can be integrated locally through CLI invocation. Existing community MCP servers demonstrate agent compatibility.

one_line_description: API service for extracting and retrieving YouTube video transcripts and captions as structured text.
auth_details: The Supadata-backed YouTube Transcript API requires an API key passed in a request header for REST API calls. Some community/free implementations claim to work without authentication.
self_serve_detail: Public developer-oriented API offerings and free tiers are referenced in public documentation and comparison pages. Community/free variants are available instantly without authentication, and commercial APIs advertise free usage tiers.
api_breadth_detail: Focused transcript retrieval API for YouTube videos, including transcript chunks and available languages endpoints. Primarily centered on caption/transcript extraction rather than broader YouTube platform functionality.
mcp_server_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist for YouTube transcript retrieval, including @fabriqa.ai/youtube-transcript-mcp on npm, kyong0612/youtube-mcp, and kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on GitHub. These support fetching transcripts from YouTube videos for Claude Code/Desktop and other MCP clients. Sources: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fabriqa.ai/youtube-transcript-mcp , https://mcpservers.org/servers/kyong0612/youtube-mcp , https://github.com/kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript
buildability_detail: A public REST API with API key authentication and self-serve/free-tier access appears available, making it feasible for Composio to build an agent toolkit today. Scope is narrow but straightforward: transcript and caption extraction.

one_line_description: AI meeting recorder and transcription platform with meeting notes and analytics.
auth_details: Grain supports OAuth2 authorization code flow with manually requested Client ID & Secret and token refresh flow. It also supports personal access tokens/workspace tokens sent as Bearer tokens in the Authorization header for Personal API access.
self_serve_detail: Public API exists and personal access tokens can be generated in a Grain account, but OAuth client credentials require manual request/approval from Grain ('Request Client ID & Secret (manually)'). Search results do not confirm fully self-serve developer onboarding.
api_breadth_detail: Public REST API for accessing meeting data, transcripts, notes, and workspace integrations. Coverage appears focused on core meeting/transcript functionality; API is described as still in beta.
mcp_server_detail: Official Grain MCP server documented at https://developers.grain.com/mcp for accessing meeting data in Claude and other MCP clients. Community MCP server also exists at https://github.com/eadm/grain-mcp-server.
buildability_blocker: OAuth app credentials require manual approval/request; API appears beta.
buildability_detail: Composio could likely build an integration today using Grain's REST API and token auth, and MCP support exists. However, OAuth onboarding is not fully self-serve because Client ID/Secret must be requested manually, and the API is still in beta.
